title: Periodic Trends in Radical-Mediated Exchange Coupling and Magnetic Anisotropy in Ln2N2 Complexes
abstract: Large crystal-field anisotropy and strong exchange interactions are key ingredients in the design of next-generation molecule-based magnetic materials. Radical-bridged lanthanide complexes are particularly promising in this regard owing to their highly anisotropic ground states and strong exchange interactions mediated by the radical bridge. Here, we present a comprehensive ab initio investigation of the magnetic and exchange anisotropy in the {[((Me3Si)2N)2(THF)Ln]2(N2)}− complexes, where Ln = Gd3+, Tb3+, Dy3+, Ho3+, and Er3+.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: Regularized Frozen Natural Orbital Approach to CASPT2: Extension to Restricted Active Space Wave Functions, Different Multiplicities and Assessment of Correlation Effects
abstract: The frozen natural orbital (FNO) method is a well-known approximation that significantly reduces the cost of many-body perturbation theory treatments for obtaining correlation energies in a systematic and controlled manner, enabling the simulation of larger and more realistic molecular systems. Here, we implement FNO on top of restricted active-space self-consistent field (RASSCF) wave functions within second-order perturbation theory, leading to the FNO-RASPT2 method. To account for the additional approximations incurred when using RASSCF wave functions, as well as to apply it to states of different molecular charge and spin multiplicity, we introduce a regularization approach via a level-shift in the orbital deletion procedure, which helps avoid singularities resulting from vanishing denominators due to the reduced occupation of restricted (active) virtual orbitals and that we show does not significantly influence the final energies obtained. Numerical results on vertical excitation energies showcase the FNO to be up to ∼4.0 times faster than the parent computation while retaining ∼95% of the dynamic correlation energy and being within 0.1 eV of the reference calculation, with the CASPT2 equations – the main bottleneck in large molecular systems – registering over an order of magnitude speed-up. An in-depth analysis shows the regularized FNO approach to retain electron correlation appropriately for internal and semi-internal contributions, while displaying larger deviations for the external term, which originates from the initial FNO truncation based on an approximated one-electron reduced density matrix. Ongoing efforts are directed toward improving and extending our current implementation to the calculation of analytic gradients and nonadiabatic couplings to enable faster nonadiabatic molecular dynamics simulations in larger and more realistic molecular systems.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: Artificial intelligence methods for HER2 status assessment: a systematic review and diagnostic meta-analysis.
abstract: Human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) is an important predictive and prognostic biomarker that guides targeted therapy, particularly in breast and gastric cancers. Conventional HER2 assessment using immunohistochemistry (IHC) and fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) is limited by inter-observer variability, heterogeneous expression, and diagnostic complexity. This systematic review and diagnostic meta-analysis followed the PRISMA 2020 guidelines to evaluate Artificial Intelligence-based HER2 assessment.

title: Local, Non-Redundant Molecular Coordinates from Disjoint Primitive Families: Symmetry-Adapted Construction and Applications
abstract: Internal coordinates express molecular motion in chemical terms, but primitive functions are redundant, and global delocalization mixes coordinate families. We introduce extended symmetry-adapted local coordinates (ESALCs), which organize diverse chemical primitives into disjoint families and complete, nonredundant bases. The internal-coordinate form, ESALC-I, assigns general primitives to perceived chemical domains, forms local symmetry-adapted combinations, selects exact rank through the Wilson B matrix, and retains complete molecular-symmetry subspaces within a basin of fixed topology and…
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: Magnetic Resonance Silent Activatable Probe with Massive Signal Amplification for Rapid Detection of Inflammation-Associated Fibrogenesis
abstract: Biomarker-specific molecular imaging is vital in precision medicine. However, a fundamental challenge of most molecular imaging methods is the difficulty of distinguishing specific molecular signal from nonspecific signal arising from the distribution of the molecular probe. This is even more pronounced in metabolically active organs such as the kidney and liver where the probe may concentrate prior to elimination. As a result, almost all molecular imaging relies on delayed imaging to achieve specificity, but this constrains clinical throughput and impedes rapid assessment of the diseased organ. Here, we report a magnetic resonance (MR) probe, Fe(II)-IAFP2, which combines 3 drivers of relaxivity enhancement to decouple disease specificity from probe distribution. Fe(II)-IAFP2 is MR-silent in its Fe(II) state, producing negligible MR signal even at high concentrations. In inflammatory, fibrogenic microenvironments common to many diseases, rapid oxidation to Fe(III) activates MR enhancement, while reversible aldehyde-mediated binding to remodeled extracellular matrix further amplifies relaxivity and promotes retention at the site of tissue injury. This dual activation–retention mechanism enables robust signal generation within minutes of administration. In mouse models of renal and liver fibrogenesis, Fe(II)-IAFP2 generated disease-associated MR contrast within minutes after intravenous administration. Together, this work demonstrates an effective strategy for rapid, activity-based molecular MR imaging through the combination of pathological activation and complementary tissue retention.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Sense-to-sense changes in bacterial genetic codes: Experimental validation by cell-free translation and native-host proteomics
abstract: In the sixty years since the publication of the complete genetic code [1], many variants of the classical codon table [2] have been observed to occur naturally, including both stop codon and sense-to-sense reassignment, but in bacteria the only experimentally validated variants are stop-codon reassignments. Recently, computational analysis with Codetta predicted bacterial genetic codes containing sense-to-sense changes. Using an Escherichia coli cell-free protein synthesis (CFPS) system, we tested tRNAs predicted to reassign arginine codons to tryptophan. These candidate CGG-decoding tRNAs from bacteria phylogenetically distant from E. coli restored cyan fluorescence from an sfGFP Y66R reporter in a dose-dependent manner when added to CFPS extracts containing canonical tRNAArg(CCG). Reactions lacking the CGG-to-Trp candidate tRNA remained near background. Reassignment was also observed with firefly luciferase and NanoLuc reporters, in which Trp incorporation restored activity and solubility. Intact-protein mass spectrometry yielded masses consistent with Arg-to-Trp substitution. Deep data-independent acquisition (DIA) proteomics of Anaerococcus prevotii, a species for which Codetta predicts CGG to code for Trp, revealed six peptides containing Trp encoded at native CGG codons and no peptides containing CGG-encoded Arg, consistent with native CGG decoding as Trp in this organism. Together, these results provide direct functional support for predicted bacterial sense-to-sense genetic codes and establish a cell-free framework for discovering natural tRNAs that expand translational coding capacity.

title: From Benign to Fatal: Native Surface Chemistry Controls Acid-Triggered Trap Landscapes in CsPbBr3 Nanocrystals
abstract: Colloidal CsPbBr3 nanocrystals can be highly emissive, yet their chemical robustness is dictated by their native surface chemistry. Here, we show that aliphatic acids interact fundamentally differently with distinct CsPbBr3 surface terminations: they are largely benign toward conventional bromine-rich ammonium-passivated surfaces but strongly destabilizing toward carboxylate-capped, Pb-rich, Br-deficient surfaces synthesized in lauric acid-menthol deep eutectic solvent (DES).

title: Explainable multi-view graph neural networks for prioritizing autism risk genes and identifying transcriptional modules
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) has a heterogeneous genetic architecture in which risk-associated genes may participate in interconnected molecular pathways. We present an graph-explainable multi-view graph neural network (GEM-GNN) for prioritizing ASD-associated genes by integrating protein-protein interaction (PPI) and brain-specific co-expression networks with genomic features.

title: SeqBattNet: A discrete-state physics-informed neural network with aging adaptation for battery modeling
abstract: Accurate battery modeling is essential for reliable state estimation in modern applications, such as predicting the remaining discharge time and remaining discharge energy in battery management systems. Existing approaches face several limitations: model-based methods require a large number of physical parameters; data-driven methods rely heavily on labeled datasets; and current physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) often lack aging adaptation, still depend on many physical parameters, or require continuous state regeneration. In this work, we propose SeqBattNet, a discrete-state PINN with built-in aging adaptation for battery modeling to predict terminal voltage during the discharge process. SeqBattNet consists of two components: (i) an encoder, implemented as the proposed Hierarchical Reasoning-GRU deep learning module, which generates cycle-specific aging adaptation parameters; and (ii) a decoder, based on the equivalent circuit model (ECM) combined with deep learning, which uses these parameters together with the input current to predict voltage. The model requires only a small number of readily available physical battery parameters and, when trained on data from a single cell, demonstrates promising predictive performance on unseen battery cells within the evaluated datasets. Experimental results on three benchmark datasets (TRI, RT-Batt, and NASA) show that SeqBattNet consistently outperforms classical sequence models and recent PINN baselines. On the NASA dataset, SeqBattNet reduces the RMSE from 0.0382 to 0.0257 for battery RW4 and from 0.0406 to 0.0253 for battery RW5 compared with the state-of-the-art PDB-Net, corresponding to relative improvements of approximately 32.7% and 37.7%.

title: Ceci n ’ est pas le benzène : The Treachery of Chemical Representations in Machine Learning for Drug Discovery
abstract: Chemists do not draw molecules; they draw agreements about molecules. A hexagon with three alternating lines is not benzene, and, read literally, it is not even an adequate model, since it localizes bonds that experiment treats as equivalent. Chemists repair this discrepancy automatically and never write the repair down; a machine receives the convention, plus whatever further theory its software compiles into it. This Perspective asks what our models actually see, across structural formulas, SMILES, fingerprints, graphs, conformers, simulated ensembles and the token sequences on which chemical language models are trained. We argue that both members of the training pair are representations─one of a chemical entity, the other of an assay-conditioned observation─and interpret tautomeric ambiguity, stereochemical and solid-form identity, activity cliffs, heterogeneous bioactivity labels and generative failure as consequences of this double reduction. We propose accountability, not realism, as the operative standard: explicit entity definitions, complementary representations, assay provenance, calibrated uncertainty, prospective testing. We then make the standard operational, setting out the controlled comparisons that separate representational loss from model limitation, sparse training coverage and experimental heterogeneity, and specifying for each perturbation test the control that makes it interpretable, the criterion for an actionable failure, and the corrective action it implies.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Ammonia-Driven Nanoscale Surface Restructuring of Copper Catalysts during Nitrate Reduction Reaction
abstract: The electrolyte and applied potential are known to impact a catalyst’s structure and performance, yet the role of reaction intermediates and products in driving surface evolution remains largely unexplored. Here, using electrochemical atomic force microscopy, we show that the dynamic restructuring of copper (Cu) surfaces during nitrate reduction reaction (NO3RR) directly correlates with the rate and selectivity of ammonia (NH3) formation. At moderate overpotentials, where nitrite formation dominates, lateral expansion of Cu terraces is observed, whereas rapid NH3 formation at higher cathodic potentials induces Cu adislands enriched in low-coordinated step sites, revealing distinct restructuring pathways that accompany the transition from nitrite- to ammonia-selective NO3RR. These transformations are rationalized by an NH3-mediated Cu dissolution-redeposition mechanism. Our results identify reaction products as active modulators of catalyst surface structure, establishing a framework for understanding reaction-driven catalyst restructuring and enabling in situ control of catalyst surfaces through the interfacial reaction environment.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Reusable molecular fabric could cut energy needed to separate industrial chemicals
abstract: Separating out a particular toxic chemical from industrial processes linked to the manufacture of nylon, paint, certain foams found in furniture and even detergents requires a lot of energy and hassle. Now a team of scientists from UT Austin and Zhejiang University has struck upon a solution that could prove far more energy efficient and practical. The research is published in the journal Nature.

title: Reprogramming ThDP-Dependent Enzyme for Intermolecular [3 + 2] Annulation via a Homoenolate Intermediate
abstract: Thiamine diphosphate (ThDP)-dependent enzymes are versatile biocatalysts for carbon–carbon bond formation, yet their catalytic repertoire has been largely confined to linear homologation and intramolecular cyclizations that rely on single-site reactive intermediates such as the Breslow or ketyl radical species. Intermolecular annulation─a powerful strategy for constructing cyclic architectures─has remained elusive within this enzyme class.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: PertiNet: Interaction-Aware Multimodal Modeling of Protein–Protein Interactions
abstract: Protein–protein interaction (PPI) prediction requires models that combine sequence, structure and functional evidence for proteins excluded from training. We developed PertiNet, which represents these inputs as separate modality tokens, models their interactions and assigns each token a protein-pair-specific weight. On the fixed protein-disjoint Bernett benchmark, PertiNet using sequence and structure achieved AUROC, AUPRC, balanced accuracy and MCC values of 0.71, 0.72, 0.66 and 0.33, respectively.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Low-Temperature-Mediated Lamellar–Micelle Assembly of Wrinkled Mesoporous Carbon Nanospheres with Aligned Pores and High Interconnectivity
abstract: Mesoporous structures with highly permeable channels are of great significance for fast diffusion; however, the delicate engineering of straightforward pores remains quite limited, with most of mesostructures are tortuous pores derived from spherical micelle assembly. Herein, we explore a novel lamellar–micelle assembly approach that enables to generate a type of wrinkled mesoporous carbon nanospheres with highly interconnected divergent mesopores.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: A Double-Tethered Metallacyclobutadiene Catalyst for Cyclic Polymer Synthesis
abstract: The synthesis, characterization, and catalytic polymerization results of an unprecedented double-tethered metallacyclobutadiene complex (4) are discussed. Complex 4 is active for the polymerization of acetylenes. Complex 4 polymerizes tert-butylacetylene to form cyclic poly(tert-butylacetylene). Evidence for a cyclic polymer topology comes from size exclusion chromatography (SEC) and intrinsic viscosity (η) measurements.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Elucidation of Pathways in the Conversion of CO2-Rich Syngas to Methanol over Cu-Based Catalysts
abstract: The efficient conversion of CO2-rich syngas to fuels remains challenging because of distinct thermodynamics between CO2 and CO hydrogenation. In this work, we investigate the structure–performance relationship and reaction mechanism of CO2-rich syngas conversion to methanol over a series of Cu-based catalysts, with CO2 contents ranging from 4% to 25%. We find that the CuZnZr catalyst exhibits the best overall performance because of the enhanced adsorption/activation of CO and CO2, resulting from the strengthened Cu–oxide interaction and promoted Cu–ZnO–ZrOx interface.

title: Acetaldehyde-Mediated Direct Conversion of Air to Nitric Acid
abstract: The sustainable synthesis of nitric acid (HNO3) directly from air via N2 oxidation is a dream reaction but remains a long-standing challenge, owing to formidable thermodynamic and kinetic barriers. Here, we report a photoassisted thermocatalytic strategy in which acetaldehyde as a key medium enables efficient N2 oxidation to HNO3 under mild conditions. Acetaldehyde is oxidized to peracetic acid over 316L stainless steel, which subsequently generates radicals (CH3COOO•) under visible-light irradiation.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Inverse Design of Potential Dicyanamide Anion Based Ionic Liquids with High Nernst–Einstein Conductivity
abstract: Ionic liquids exhibit wide electrochemical windows, negligible volatility, and strong design flexibility, making them promising electrolytes for next-generation energy storage devices. However, the vast design space renders conventional trial-and-error discovery inefficient. Here, we develop a reinforcement learning framework for the de novo inverse design of potential dicyanamide-anion-based ionic liquids with enhanced Nernst–Einstein conductivity. A recurrent neural network trained on known cation structures was coupled with Monte Carlo tree search to generate novel cations.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Interpreting and Validating a Deep Learning Model Predictive of Spatial Morphologic-Molecular Patterns in Lung Adenocarcinoma, Using Ground Truth Immunohistochemistry Images.
abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD), the most common subtype of non-small cell lung cancer, exhibits profound histological and molecular heterogeneity. While genomic profiling has identified key oncogenic drivers and immune signatures, its use is limited by cost, technical demands and tissue availability. In addition, spatial transcriptomics provides spatially resolved molecular insights but remains challenging and time-consuming.

title: A noninvasive risk stratification prediction model for neuroblastoma through integration of multidimensional clinical indicators.
abstract: Current neuroblastoma (NB) risk classification relies partly on tumor tissue-derived information, which may be unavailable in patients who cannot undergo biopsy or surgical resection. Therefore, this study aimed to develop a non-invasive prediction model for NB risk classification by integrating a liquid biopsy biomarker with routinely available clinical indicators. A total of 141 treatment-naïve patients with NB were included and divided into a training cohort (n = 100) and a held-out testing cohort (n = 41).

title: A Molybdoenzyme Mediates Carbon–Sulfur Bond Making and Breaking in Ergothioneine Biosynthesis
abstract: The molybdopterin-dependent ergothioneine synthase (MES) from Caldithrix abyssi is the first molybdoenzyme known to catalyze the formation of carbon–sulfur bonds. To complete its catalytic cycle, this bifunctional enzyme desulfurates l-cysteine at a pyridoxal 5′-phosphate binding site and transfers the harvested sulfur atom (S0) to the molybdenum center of a bis-molybdopterin guanine dinucleotide cofactor more than 50 Å away. Subsequently, the sulfurated Mo-center transfers the labile sulfur atom onto the imidazole ring of Nα-trimethyl histidine (TMH). Combining experimental observations from cryo-electron microscopy, X-ray crystallography, X-ray absorption spectroscopy, sequence-activity correlation, and substrate-specificity studies, we delineate the structural basis for long-distance sulfur transfer via a persulfide relay, the identity of the imidazole sulfurating species, and key sequence motifs that are indispensable for activity. Furthermore, the reversibility of MES-mediated sulfurization of TMH under physiological conditions suggests that ergothioneine may serve as a soluble reservoir of oxidizing equivalents, supporting anaerobic metabolism in deep-branching bacteria such as C. abyssi.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Accumulation characteristics, driving mechanisms, and simulation prediction of PAHs in soils surrounding typical industrial parks in Beijing.
abstract: Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs) accumulate persistently in soils around industrial parks, yet most studies capture only a static snapshot and overlook how contamination evolves. Shifting from static assessment to accumulation dynamics, we tracked PAH accumulation across three campaigns (2018, 2022, 2026) around four industrial parks in Beijing, identified its drivers, and developed an interpretable, scenario-based prediction model. The average Σ16PAHs was 1.01 mg/kg; high-molecular-weight (4- to 5-ring) PAHs were abundant, and benzo[a]pyrene contributed 45.26% of the toxicity risk.

title: Role of (Co)substrate Coordination to Iron in Activating Its Two-Electron Reduction of Dioxygen: Mechanism of Pterin Activation in Tryptophan Hydroxylase
abstract: Many O2-activating mononuclear nonheme iron enzymes require substrate or cofactor/cosubstrate coordination to iron to form the key peroxy-bridged intermediate necessary for catalysis with no net change in the iron redox state. The role of (co)substrate coordination, however, remained unclear. Here, we leverage a pterin-dependent enzyme, tryptophan hydroxylase, for which cosubstrate (pterin) coordination can be experimentally controlled by the absence and presence of substrate, to explicitly determine the role of pterin coordination in O2 binding and peroxo formation. EPR, absorption, circular dichroism, and magnetic circular dichroism spectroscopies on the {FeNO}7 analog of the unobservable {FeO2}8 intermediate without and with pterin coordination demonstrate that pterin coordination induces new absorption bands and enhances NO affinity by 3.6 kcal mol–1 at 277 K. These new bands are pterin-to-iron ligand-to-metal charge-transfer transitions that compensate the electron donation from iron to NO upon NO binding. Extension of our findings on {FeNO}7 to {FeO2}8 evidences that pterin coordination stabilizes O2 binding and facilitates the two-electron transfer from pterin to {FeO2}8 to reduce the transition-state barrier for peroxo formation by 12.7 kcal mol–1, corresponding to a 1010 increase in reaction rate. The electron transfer pathways established herein underscore a unified mechanism for the pterin-dependent, α-ketoglutarate-dependent, extradiol, and intradiol dioxygenase families of mononuclear nonheme iron enzymes through which (co)substrate coordination enhances O2 binding via one-electron transfer within {FeO2}8 and two-electron donation from the (co)substrate (one to bound O2 and one to iron) to generate the peroxo species with no net redox change on the iron.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: A Crystalline LaCl3 Reinforced Amorphous Oxyhalide Electrolyte for Thermally Stable All-Solid-State Batteries
abstract: All-solid-state batteries (ASSBs) are a promising next-generation energy storage technology, but their development is often constrained by the thermal instability and high cost of solid-state electrolytes (SSEs). Amorphous oxyhalide electrolytes, while mechanically deformable, are particularly susceptible to thermal degradation. Here, we report a novel and cost-effective composite SSE fabricated by embedding LaCl3 nanocrystals within an amorphous Li–Al–O–Cl (LAOC) matrix.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Bioinformatics and In Vivo Experiments Identify Hmgcs2 as a Key Gene Linking Fatty Acid Metabolism and Lactylation in Acute Kidney Injury Associated with Sepsis
abstract: Background Sepsis-associated acute kidney injury (S-AKI) is a severe critical care complication with high morbidity and mortality, involving inflammatory dysregulation, metabolic reprogramming, and immune dysfunction. However, the molecular link between fatty acid metabolism disorders and lactylation in S-AKI remains unclear, and systematic screening with functional validation is lacking. Methods Based on mouse kidney transcriptome datasets, we performed DEGs analysis, GSEA, GO/KEGG enrichment, and LASSO regression to screen key candidates.

title: Visible-Light-Driven Dearomatization via Electrocyclic Ring Expansion for Solar Energy Storage
abstract: Molecular solar thermal (MOST) energy storage compounds capture solar photon energy in the strained chemical bonds of metastable photoisomers and release it on demand as heat, yet simultaneously achieving visible-light absorption and high energy storage density has remained a persistent challenge. Here we introduce 9-aryl acridine N-oxides as MOST compounds based on visible-light-driven dearomative ring expansion.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Solvent/Anion Codepleted Solvation Engineering Enables Low-Coordination Electrolytes for High-Energy and Low-Temperature Sodium-Ion Pouch Cells
abstract: Widespread deployment of sodium-ion batteries demands both high energy density and reliable low-temperature (LT) operation, but is constrained by a persistent trade-off between high-voltage stability (cathode/electrolyte) and LT ion-transport kinetics. Herein, we report a solvent/anion codepleted solvation engineering strategy to construct low-coordination electrolytes through competitive anion complexation mediated by a bulky electron-deficient additive, TMSB (tris(trimethylsilyl)borate).
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Palladium(II)-Catalyzed Denitrogenation of Alkyl Diazirines
abstract: [PdCl2(NCPh)2] catalyzes the denitrogenation of mono(alkyl) diazirines in CDCl3 at 25 °C for 16 h to form the corresponding alkene in up to 70% yield. Reaction of (4-fluorophenyl)diazirine with a catalytic amount of [PdCl2(NCPh)2] (20 mol %) and excess styrene forms 1-(4-fluorophenyl)-2-phenylcyclopropane in 48% yield (cis/trans = 6.7:1). Kinetic experiments, in situ analysis of palladium coordination complexes, and DFT calculations support a mechanism for Pd(II)-catalyzed denitrogenation of benzyl diazirine involving C─N oxidative addition (ΔG‡ = 22.4 kcal/mol) of a four-coordinate…

title: Synergistic Bifunctional Sites Catalysis in Atomically Mixed Ir x Os1− x Nanoparticles for Efficient NO Reduction by CO
abstract: The development of cost-effective alternatives to rhodium for catalytic NO reduction by CO remains urgent and challenging. Here, we report the synthesis of atomically mixed IrxOs1−x solid-solution nanoparticles across the full compositional range. The optimized Ir0.4Os0.6/γ-Al2O3 catalyst achieved a temperature at 50% conversion of 214 °C, far surpassing those of monometallic Ir (300 °C) and Os (266 °C) and rivaling a commercial Rh benchmark. Their activities exhibited a clear volcano-type dependence on the Ir content.

title: Machine learning methods to decipher the evolutionary dynamics of microbial pathogens.
abstract: We are currently witnessing an unprecedented rise in the amount of diverse data on pathogens and epidemics. These data include genomic sequences with metadata such as geographic locations, risk groups, and sampling information. Machine learning (ML) has been applied to overcome the scalability bottlenecks inherent in these heterogeneous and high-dimensional datasets.

title: Enteric Neuroglia-Immune Axis in Dysbiosis: Modulating the Tripartite Cascade with Dietary Phytochemicals
abstract: The gastrointestinal tract is a dynamic regulatory interface in which the enteric nervous system (ENS), supported by an extensive enteric glial cell (EGC) network, interacts with the enteric immune system (EIS) and gut microbiota to maintain epithelial barrier integrity, neuroplasticity, motility, and tissue repair. In eubiosis, coordinated signaling across this tripartite axis supports intestinal homeostasis.

title: Photomediated Chromium-Catalyzed Regio-, Diastereo-, and Enantioselective Deoxygenative Coupling of Activated Allylic and Propargylic Alcohols with Aldehydes
abstract: Chromium-catalyzed asymmetric Nozaki–Hiyama–Kishi (NHK) reaction is a powerful tool for constructing synthetically valuable enantioenriched homoallylic alcohols and allenols. However, catalytic asymmetric NHK-type coupling of allylic or propargylic C–O electrophiles remains largely underdeveloped. Herein, we report a photomediated chromium-catalyzed deoxygenative coupling of activated allylic and propargylic alcohols with aldehydes, enabling the synthesis of a variety of chiral homoallylic alcohols with wide structural diversity and allenols.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: High-Quality InSb Nanowires Grown by Molecular-Beam Epitaxy via Precise Catalyst Modulation
abstract: Semiconductor InSb nanowires are a major material candidate for topological quantum computation. The nanowires in current devices were mostly grown using metal organic chemical vapor deposition, incompatible with in situ growth of superconductor, a crucial requirement for low-disorder devices. Growth of InSb nanowires using molecular-beam epitaxy (MBE) can address this issue. So far, studies on MBE-grown InSb remain limited due to an extremely narrow parameter window for the growth and reproducibility. Moreover, the use of foreign catalysts can introduce deep-level impurities. Here, we report a self-catalyzed MBE growth of InSb nanowires without those foreign catalysts. We first grow GaAs nanowire stems, and then convert Ga catalyst droplets into In droplets in situ. Axial heteroepitaxial growth of InSb can be realized through the In droplets on top of GaAs stems. We further find that a low flux suppresses radial growth, enabling linear length tuning from 0.8 to 2.6 micrometer with growth time, while diameter stays nearly constant. These InSb nanowires have a pure zinc-blende structure free of twins, stacking faults. Transport measurement reveals an electron mobility near 19000 cm2 V-1s-1. Moreover, the observation of quasi-ballistic transport, quantum dots, and Kondo correlations demonstrates the coherent quantum transport capability of the MBE-grown InSb nanowires. Our work provides a substrate-independent, self-catalyzed route for the controllable synthesis of high-quality InSb nanowires, establishing a robust material platform for high-performance InSb-based electronic and quantum devices.

title: Artificial Intelligence in EGFR-mutated NSCLC: Reframing the Therapeutic and Biological Landscape
abstract: Despite advances in targeted therapy, acquired resistance to osimertinib remains a major challenge in epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutated non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC), owing to its biological heterogeneity, temporal evolution, and increasing therapeutic complexity. This narrative review critically examines the potential of artificial intelligence (AI) to integrate clinical, molecular, imaging, and pharmacological data across the osimertinib treatment trajectory, with particular emphasis on resistance monitoring and clinical pharmacology.

title: Long-lived light-driven bimagnons at finite momentum in NiO
abstract: Light can manipulate magnetic order and its excitations on ultrafast timescales, including through resonantly driven phonons. In antiferromagnets, light can also create correlated magnon pairs, or bimagnons. Unlike single magnons, whose damping has been measured and modeled in detail, little is known about the lifetime, interactions and decay of such correlated pairs: prior two-magnon measurements show broad linewidths or coherences that dephase within 200 fs. Here we pump the phonon-assisted two-magnon absorption of NiO with mid-infrared pulses, far below its bandgap, and probe the resulting magnetic dynamics at finite momentum with time-resolved resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS). Upon photoexcitation, the one-magnon linewidth and energy are essentially unchanged, indicating that the long-range magnetic order is preserved without the photocarrier-induced demagnetization characteristic of above-bandgap excitation. A pump-induced two-magnon signal appears on the energy-gain (anti-Stokes) side of the spectrum. Its spectral weight peaks 4 ps after the pump, well beyond our 0.5 ps time resolution, indicative of a delayed growth likely due to momentum redistribution of the light-induced magnon pairs across the Brillouin zone. This two-magnon signal decays with a time constant of $28\pm11$ ps, exceeding the previously reported two-magnon dephasing time by more than two orders of magnitude. These results establish long-lived light-driven bimagnon correlations beyond the one-magnon state, akin to the higher-order correlations measured in ultracold gases.

title: Toward Multilayer Architectures in Transition-Metal/Main-Group Cluster Oxides: Ir3Sn12In3O14, Ir2.3Ru1.7Sn19O18 and Ir10Sn45O44A Homologous Series with Progressive Band Condensation
abstract: A series of cluster oxides exhibiting a systematic increase in the degree of band condensation was synthesized by the reactive Sn-flux method: Ir3Sn12In3O14 (3-fold band), Ir2.3Ru1.7Sn19O18 (4-fold band), and Ir10Sn45O44 (5-fold band). Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals that these compounds crystallize in the noncentrosymmetric polar space groups Cm and Cmc21 and the centrosymmetric space group C2/m, respectively.

title: Unraveling Molybdenum Dissolution-Induced Surface Reconstruction of Cobalt Molybdenum Oxide Electrocatalysts during the Oxygen Evolution Reaction
abstract: Understanding and controlling the evolution of electrocatalyst structure, chemistry, and active sites under catalytically relevant conditions is critical in developing electrocatalysts with stable and durable activity toward the oxygen evolution reaction (OER). Molybdenum (Mo) is routinely combined with cobalt hydroxide electrocatalysts to tune the electronic environment of the active sites and modulate their activity, contributing to improved OER activity. However, the phenomena that underpin the enhanced OER activity of the resulting materials largely stem from Mo dissolution, and their extent on the structure and activity remains elusive. In this work, we investigate cobalt-molybdenum oxide electrocatalysts, CoMoOx, synthesized via the electrodeposition method across a range of Co/Mo compositional ratios and CoMoO4(HT) synthesized hydrothermally, to establish how composition and synthesis route govern Co-site evolution and the ensuing OER activity. Electrochemical benchmarking revealed that the high Mo content of electrodeposited CoMoOx(1:4) produces a Mo-rich surface with fewer accessible Co sites and slower charge-transfer kinetics, as evidenced by a Tafel slope of 73.1 ± 8.1 mV dec−1 and a high charge-transfer resistance of 5.74 Ω (over 4 times higher than CoMoOx(6:1)). Operando Raman spectroscopy, ex situ X-ray diffraction, X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and inductively coupled plasma−optical emission spectroscopy collectively demonstrate that MoO42− dissolution begins on contact with 1 M KOH in the absence of applied potential and continues under anodic polarization, driving irreversible reconstruction of as-synthesized materials to Co(OH)2/Co3O4 sites and subsequently to CoOOH. These materials therefore function as pre-catalysts, and the working surface is determined by the starting composition rather than being the as-synthesized phase. Crucially, the reconstruction pathway is synthesis-dependent; crystalline hydrated CoMoO4(HT) proceeds via CoOOH to further-oxidized, partially deprotonated CoOOHx, at relevant OER conditions, whereas electrodeposited films form predominantly β-CoOOH as the surface species, with progression beyond CoOOH developing only partially and to an extent that scales with the initial Mo content. These findings provide a mechanistic blueprint for leveraging controlled cation dissolution to engineer defect-rich, high-performance electrocatalytic interfaces.

title: Open foundation models for clinical AI

Development and clinical validation of a multiplex PCR-based targeted next-generation sequencing panel for simultaneous DNA/RNA pathogen detection in respiratory tract infections: a comprehensive performance evaluation
abstract: ObjectivesLower respiratory tract infections (LRTI) remain a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, with approximately 62 % of cases lacking definitive etiological diagnoses via conventional methods. This study aimed to develop and validate a multiplex PCR-based targeted next-generation sequencing (mp-tNGS) panel for comprehensive pathogen detection in respiratory samples.MethodsWe conducted a combined retrospective (n=209) and prospective (n=256) study involving 465 bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) samples from patients with suspected LRTI.

title: Circular phonons generate negligible magnetization in insulators
abstract: The optical excitation of circular phonons has opened up non-equilibrium phenomena with no equilibrium counterparts, ranging from the generation of synthetic magnetic fields to the control of topological order or the manipulation of ferroaxial states. In this area, significant controversy has arisen on whether sizeable "true" magnetizations accompany circular phonons. Several confounding factors cloud the interpretation of the experiments, which are based on probing polarization rotation in the driven material. These range from the interpretation of the Faraday effect in non-equilibrium conditions to spurious nonlinear optical contributions in pump probe experiments. Here we resolve these ambiguities by measuring both polarization rotation inside the driven material and the stray magnetic field generated outside it with a proximate Faraday detector. For a 5 MV/cm mid-infrared drive, we observe a colossal polarization rotation inside a driven SiC crystal, similar to what was reported in previous work. Depending on the assumptions made, this could correspond to magnetizations as high as $μ_0 M = 0.3 T$ or as low as 4 $μT$. However, when measuring the magnetic stray field outside the driven sample we unambiguously determine that the magnetization in SiC is negligibly small ($μ_0 M \lt 0.001 T$).

title: Active-space construction in single-fragment coupled-cluster embedding for chemical reactions
abstract: We benchmark single-fragment quantum embedding, in which electron correlation---at the level of coupled-cluster theory with single, double, and perturbative triple excitations [CCSD(T)]---is restricted to orbitals associated with a chosen molecular fragment, and the remaining orbitals are frozen at the Hartree-Fock level. We compare several methods for constructing fragment active spaces, and we test their performance on 60 organic reaction energies and three reaction profiles. A common fragment projection operator is used to relate several of the tested orbital constructions. Regional embedding, based on density matrix embedding theory, is shown to give accurate and robust performance when used for both the occupied and virtual active orbitals. For virtual orbitals, fragment-centered projected atomic orbitals and fragment natural orbitals (defined by eigenvectors of a fragment MP2 density matrix) also perform well, but the latter typically retains larger virtual spaces. Composite MP2 corrections yield the largest improvement: combined with fragment natural orbitals, they give average reaction energy errors below 0.3 kcal/mol relative to full-system CCSD(T), with all individual errors below 1 kcal/mol. Reaction profiles show that accurate endpoint energies can conceal substantial barrier errors, emphasizing the importance of approximating omitted correlation.

title: Inter-Nanoparticle Repulsion Effect on Self-Organization in Polymer Nanocomposites: A Langevin Dynamics Simulation Study
abstract: Demixing through liquid-liquid phase separation is relevant to nanoparticle (NP) aggregation in polymer nanocomposites (PNCs), biomolecular compartmentalization, and liquids embedded in elastic networks. Mixing-demixing phase behavior depends on factors, such as particle size distribution, system dimen-sionality, intermolecular interactions, and relative concentrations. Here, using Langevin Dynamics simu-lations, we systematically investigate the effect of inter-nanoparticle repulsion on the self-assembly of PNCs under extreme confinement. A nanoparticle assembly, in the form of a compact droplet, is immersed in a polymer matrix of semiflexible, rod-like chains. By varying the nanoparticle-nanoparticle repulsion strength, while fixing all other interactions, we identify four distinct regimes with respect to the self-assembled NP morphologies: droplet, slab, crystalline droplet, and dispersed. Cluster-based analysis reveals a progressive loss of nanoparticle droplet integrity, leading to fragmentation within the dispersed regime. Local order of the nanoparticle assembly and global order of polymer chains are gauged through refined descriptors, quantifying the degrees of crystallinity and of nematic order, respectively. Interest-ingly, the slab regime exhibits negligible nanoparticle crystallization yet demonstrates the strongest polymer nematic ordering. In contrast, the crystalline droplet displays extensive triangular close-packed crystallites accompanied by a significant reduction in polymer nematic order, owing to its rhomboid shape. In the dispersed regime, nanoparticle fragmentation facilitates efficient mixing and local smectic-like ordering of the polymer chains. These findings demonstrate that fine-tuning inter-NP repulsions can control self-organization and the resulting morphologies, providing insights into PNCs with tailored functionality.

title: JOINTS: Classification and analytical evaluation of detachable dry connections for reusable concrete elements
abstract: This paper presents a systematic classification for detachable dry joints suitable for the structural reuse of reinforced concrete elements, together with an analytical evaluation of representative configurations. The classification, named JOINTS and applicable to concrete connections beyond the reuse context, organizes the design space along five categories whose initials spell JOINT: the Juxtaposition (spatial arrangement of the paired elements), the Origin (their prior structural function), the Interface geometry, the Newly introduced materials at the joint, and the force-Transfer mechanism. A sixth category, the Score, completes the acronym and evaluates each configuration for sustainability, cost-efficiency, and mechanical performance. From this design space, three representative configurations are evaluated analytically under active post-tensioning, differing in both their joint geometry (planar, stepped, and angled) and their tendon inclination. The evaluation covers failure of the anchorage of the post-tensioning member, the contact limit of the interface, and the material limit of the concrete adjacent to the interface. Although complex joint geometries theoretically enhance interlocking, their benefit is limited by the compressive-shear strength of the concrete. The reinforcement of the reused elements may be damaged near the cut, and the splitting reinforcement that a conventional design would require is not guaranteed to exist. The present analysis therefore conservatively assumes that the concrete at the joint face alone resists the combined compression and shear, neglecting any residual contribution from the existing reinforcement. This analytical evaluation represents a first step toward quantifying the score over a parametric range of connections, here focusing on the mechanical criterion.

title: Quantum Boltzmann Equation for Static Correlation with Cumulant Kernel Closure
abstract: We present a Quantum Boltzmann Equation for static correlation by mapping the Bogoliubov-Born-Green-Kirkwood-Yvon hierarchy to discrete atomic-orbital matrix mechanics via the Wigner-Weyl isomorphism to evaluate scattering of the correlated two-body cumulant. This Quantum Boltzmann Equation converges to the active-space static correlation limit and preserves pure $N$-representability constraints during the kinetic relaxation. To resolve scaling bottlenecks of explicit two-body cumulant methods, we project the two-body cumulant onto its lowest unitary invariant and evaluate a susceptibility-windowed orbital scattering scale via a single Coulomb-exchange contraction. Relaxing onto a hyperbolic-tangent cumulant attractor through Markovian collisional relaxation yields a parameter-free Quantum Boltzmann Equation Cumulant-Kernel that regularizes derivative cusps without thermal smearing. Using the collinear $\mathrm{H}_3$ exchange reaction, the symmetric $D_{4h}$ square $\mathrm{H}_4$ dissociation, the non-adiabatic avoided crossing in $\mathrm{BeH}_2$, the symmetric bond cleavage of $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$, the triple-bond dissociation of $\mathrm{N}_2$, the 11-molecule MR-MGN-BE17 dissociation test set, and the singlet diradical isomers of benzyne as case studies, we show that this kinetic relaxation resolves strong static correlation at zero electronic temperature.

title: Programming Quantum Circuit Parameters with Large Language Models
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have recently demonstrated the ability to generate parameters for variational quantum circuits without conventional optimization. However, the conditions under which this approach is effective remain unclear. Here, we investigate a frozen, general-purpose LLM that generates complete circuit parameter vectors from symbolic circuit and Hamiltonian descriptions, with optional iterative energy feedback. We evaluate the approach on general random Hamiltonians, structured parent Hamiltonians, and molecular systems. For general Hamiltonians, LLM-generated parameters exhibit larger energy errors than conventional Adam optimization, while additional feedback generally provides limited improvement. In contrast, for structured Hamiltonians, the LLM can generate promising low-energy parameter configurations, suggesting that identifiable physical and mathematical structure facilitates parameter inference. We also show that direct LLM predictions of minimum energies can violate the Hamiltonian spectral lower bound, whereas generated circuit parameters allow independent evaluation of physically realizable energy expectation values. Finally, we investigate blind circuit interpretation and find that the LLM can predict measurement outcomes even when it fails to identify the underlying quantum algorithm. These findings highlight the role of problem structure, the limitations of iterative LLM optimization, and the importance of independently verifiable predictions in quantum parameter programming.

title: SiC-BN composites with extreme thermal and environmental stability
abstract: Ceramic materials that maintain structural integrity and resist thermal-shock under extreme conditions are critical for many applications. Here we show that spark plasma sintered composites containing equal weight fractions of hexagonal silicon carbide (6H-SiC) and boron nitride (h-BN) exhibit exceptional stability under extreme high-temperature oxidizing conditions and unusually stable temperature-independent thermal conductivity across a broad temperature range. Under high-velocity oxygen-fuel torch exposure in air, it withstands prolonged heating and thermal-cycling at surface temperatures reaching >1500 °C, whereas pure 6H-SiC and h-BN rapidly fractures or erodes. Microstructural evaluation shows the formation of a multi-phase surface silica layer that further protects the material from oxidation. Finite-element analysis heat-flux map shows that intrinsic porosity mitigates thermal stress, while ReaxFF molecular dynamics simulations reveal thermally driven interfacial reconstruction and the formation of a Si-N/C-B-rich bonding network, enhancing the interfacial cohesion at elevated temperatures. This lightweight, easily machinable ceramic composite will be a promising structural material in extreme environment applications.

title: Interplay of diffusive and active motion governs cohesin extrusion and CTCF barrier function
abstract: Cohesin-mediated loop extrusion constitutes a crucial process for the regulation of chromosome folding and gene expression. A rapidly-growing body of in vitro experiments suggests that cohesin molecular motor activity is finely modulated by both chemical and mechanical cues, whose interplay holds important implications in living cells for development and disease. Yet, biophysical models capable of accurately and efficiently capturing the breadth of reported cohesin behaviors, along with their impacts on DNA spatio-temporal organisation, remain lacking. Here, building on multiple experimental observations of single-cohesin dynamics, we introduce a mesoscale description of cohesin based on the general framework of jump-diffusion processes. We show that the finite stall force of cohesin naturally emerges from the conjunction of active, directional extrusion moves with passive, stochastic drift. The tension-dependent competition between these two orthogonal modes of motion gives rise to highly-heterogeneous cohesin kinetics featuring extrusion, translocation, and loop slipping phases, as observed in vitro. These behaviors are predicted to depend sensitively on both buffer composition and nucleosomal content, reconciling the surprising variability of cohesin kinetics reported across experimental conditions. This jump-diffusion model (JDM) is fully parametrized using available single-molecule measurements and bridges the timescale gap between microscopic stepping events and cohesin regulator association, thus providing mechanistic insights into how CTCF impedes extrusion. Hence, the JDM quantitatively describes force-dependent extrusion in both DNA curtain assays in vitro and in the context of native chromatin for genome folding predictions in nucleo, bridging these previously disparate contexts under a unified numerical and theoretical formalism.

title: Grand-Canonical Path Reweighting for Constant-Potential Langevin Dynamics
abstract: Constant-potential molecular dynamics provides an important framework for studying the structural, thermodynamic, and kinetic properties of electrochemical systems at a prescribed electrochemical potential, but independent simulations under different electrochemical conditions can be computationally demanding, particularly for rare-event kinetics. Here, we develop a trajectory reweighting framework based on extended-phase-space Langevin dynamics, in which the electron number Ne is treated as an additional dynamical degree of freedom and the nuclear and electronic degrees of freedom evolve…
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: Future directions of nanocatalysts in precision medicine: from catalytic therapy to intelligent nanozymes
abstract: The scope of nanomedicine may be broadened by nanocatalysts, which can actively modulate biochemical reactions in vivo. Of these nanocatalysts, nanozymes (nanomaterials with intrinsic enzyme-like activity) probably have received the most attention. Their activity can catalyze a reaction similar to peroxidase, catalase, oxidase, superoxide dismutase, or glutathione peroxidase, depending on composition, thus generating or scavenging reactive oxygen species (ROS) depending on the microenvironment. This review sketches the evolution of this field from first generation iron oxide nanozymes to more recent stimuli-responsive multi-enzyme nanostructures. Moreover, selected experimental studies are examined, starting from in vivo Fenton and Fenton-like chemodynamic therapy and cascade catalysis and oxygen-releasing nanozymes in cancer, to antioxidant, antimicrobial, and immunomodulatory nanozymes in regenerative medicine, neurological, cardiovascular, and infectious disease models, respectively. For every case, the specific nanozyme, the biological model, the proposed mechanism of action, and the primary results are outlined, while the amount of evidence supporting the work is rated. The challenges for translating these systems into the clinic are addressed, such as the selectivity of the catalytic process to the physiological H2O2 concentration, efficiency of biodistribution, availability of long-term safety studies, batch-to-batch consistency, and ambiguity on regulatory pathways. It is speculated which of these issues can be practically solved by machine learning and which are more resistant. Future strategies are envisioned in creating biohybrid, logic-gated nanozymes, omics-guided design, and in vitro autonomous discovery platforms. CLINICAL TRIAL REGISTRATION: Not applicable. This study does not involve any clinical trial and does not require trial registration.

title: Chemical crosslinking enables profiling of endogenous cell surface galectin-3 interactions
abstract: Galectin-3 is a {beta}-galactoside-binding lectin that organizes glycoproteins into cell surface lattices (multivalent interaction networks) that regulate biology spanning immune function, fibrosis, heart disease, and cancer progression. Galectin-3 engages promiscuous but low-affinity glycan ligands, posing technical challenges for faithfully mapping the cell surface galectin-3 interactome. Here, we introduce Crosslinking-assisted Galectin Lattice Affinity Purification Mass Spectrometry (xGL-APMS), a facile and stringent proteome-scale approach that captures galectin-3 interactions natively at the cell surface, without the need for exogenous galectin-3, and is extendable to XL-MS. We identified 125 N-glycan branching-dependent surface galectin-3 interactors on Jurkat cells, validated interactions with six orthogonal approaches, and compared low and high-dose galectin-3 interactomes, revealing differences in both distribution and interactome composition. Finally, without exogenous or modified bait, we performed immediate crosslinking of endogenous galectin-3 to identify 69 galectin-3-associated proteins on primary mouse thymocytes. Together, these approaches provide a readily adoptable framework for measuring endogenous surface galectin-3 and profiling its interacting partners.

title: Aging Remodels the Female Skeletal Muscle Proteome Toward Matrix, Chromatin and Lysosomal Programs that Track Loss of Physical Function
abstract: Loss of skeletal muscle strength and mobility is among the most consequential features of human aging, yet the molecular programs that accompany this decline in women remain poorly understood. Here, we performed deep comprehensive data-independent acquisition (DIA) proteomic profiling of vastus lateralis biopsies from 10 younger (24-30 years) and 10 older (70-84 years) healthy women enrolled through the NIH Common Fund Cellular Senescence Network (SenNet), with matched measurements of grip strength and gait speed.

title: Symmetry in Time: A Representation Theory of Linear Recurrent Memory
abstract: State space models (SSMs) are an emerging alternative to Transformers. SSMs offer linear-time inference and parallel training, but most implementations make the parallel scan efficient by making the recurrence diagonal: each channel of the hidden state is multiplied by an input-dependent real or complex number. These numbers commute, so the state records which inputs occurred but not their order. We formalize this with representation theory, which explains and fixes the state-tracking failures previously reported for SSMs. The state update defines a linear representation of the monoid of input sequences, and we show that an SSM tracks a group at every sequence length exactly when that group is a quotient of the group generated by its transition matrices. Two consequences follow. Diagonal real- and complex-valued SSMs can track only commutative groups, while the transition matrices of any SSM that can track a group must split into independent blocks over the real, complex, and quaternion numbers. We then introduce HyperSSM, which adds quaternion channels while keeping linear-time inference and parallel training. Trained only on final answers, HyperSSM solves the group tasks of recent state-tracking benchmarks exactly with at most five state numbers. This includes $S_5$ with 32 generators, where previous SSMs are at chance, and HyperSSM generalizes to sequences 25 times longer than those seen in training. Because the theory says what the transitions must encode, the learned weights of the linear recurrence can be interpreted directly. We demonstrate this by recovering the calibration of a real gyroscope, the rotations of imperfect qubit gates and the geometry of protein backbones.

title: Using an energy pixels approach to estimate the size a 2nd Generation DEL must be to train a high-resolution binding model
abstract: DNA-encoded libraries (DELs) are commonly used to find small-molecule binders to a target protein. But the hard part is no longer finding a hit. It is building a machine-learning model good enough to guide the medicinal chemistry that follows, one that can resolve the shift in affinity when a chemist changes a single atom. Such a model needs two things from its training data: dense sampling of the small patch of chemical space around the hit, and an adequate number of genuinely tight binders within it. A diverse naive DEL gives neither. It samples an enormous space, so any one neighborhood is covered far too thinly, and the tightest binders are rare. A model trained on that naive DEL data must extrapolate to binders tighter than any it has seen, and that is where models can fail. One way to get training data with both properties is a second-generation DEL built around the hit. We ask how complex that library must be. We treat binding as a sum of small, independent interactions, called pixels on the target and antipixels on the ligand. From the spread of affinities measured in the naive library, with no structural information and nothing yet synthesized, we estimate the complexity such a library must have to supply that dense sampling and those tight binders. The method does two useful things. It turns the number of tight binders a model needs into the number of compounds a library must contain. And it estimates the expected yield of a randomly designed second-generation DEL, so the gain from designing the library with machine learning or active learning can be measured against a baseline, without the expense of a control library as large as the experiment itself.

title: Library of peptides: Analysis of a complex reactive mixture with the use of statistical physics and inference
abstract: Self-assembled mixtures enable the exploration of vast chemical diversity, yet characterizing the hundreds of coexisting species they contain remains a major challenge. Standard analytical techniques such as chromatography and spectroscopy produce overlapping signals that cannot be resolved by conventional deconvolution methods, which neglect the concentration correlations imposed by the reactive network. Here, we introduce a framework that bridges statistical physics and analytical chemistry to deconvolute complex self-assembled mixtures from partial spectral data. Inspired by Potts models of protein folding, we express the chemical potential of each compound as a function of a reduced set of parameters-intrinsic building-block energies and pairwise coupling terms between neighboring building blocks in the sequence. Coupling this model with the law of mass action yields equilibrium concentrations across the entire reactive network. The model parameters can be infered by fitting predicted spectroscopic signals to experimentally measured partial data. We demonstrate this approach using dynamic combinatorial libraries (DCLs) of peptides as a model system. Applied to a DCL of 81 peptides, our method resolves the full mixture composition from just 13 overlapping peaks, revealing that lateral couplings dominate the assembly energetics. Beyond DCLs, this strategy offers a general route for analyzing self-assembled systems from partial data and extends naturally to target-driven identification of high-affinity binders.

title: Physically Interpretable Basin Selection in Discrete-Variable Origami Design
abstract: Automatic differentiation has enabled rapid progress on continuous-variable mechanical design problems, but gradient-based optimization still struggles with discrete variables. The standard approach is to optimize using a continuous relaxation of the choices, then commit to the nearest discrete design at the end. Why this procedure selects unfavorable basins is poorly understood. Here, we introduce a practical, interpretable design problem inspired by origami, in which automatic differentiation is used to design shapes with a target functional behavior. Each origami sheet has a fixed geometry, and a bilevel optimization framework tunes which one of four discrete hinge types to place at each fold. Baseline gradient-based design settles into basins with a large discretization gap: relaxed optimization solves 97% of runs, but the final, discrete solutions succeed only half the time. We find that the gap can be relieved with a surprisingly simple modification. An initialization prior uniformly biased toward the stiff, flat hinge option boosts the final solve fraction from 49% to 69%. Applying the prior adds no additional compute and leaves the optimization process unchanged. Compared to the baseline, sheets produced with the prior have greater geometric compatibility and mechanical stiffness. Directly penalizing frustration and floppiness in the outer loss function produces an even greater improvement than the prior does, raising the solve fraction to 78% and indicating that these properties help distinguish the unfavorable basins. Our results demonstrate that loss landscapes for mechanical design can have physically meaningful basins that are not robust to discretization and cause solves to fail. Targeting these basins' physical signatures, even with just an initialization bias, helps avoid them.

title: How potentials and electric fields together control reactions on catalyst surfaces
abstract: Researchers at the Interface Science Department (ISC) have shown that electrochemical reactions at solid-solution interfaces can be impacted by two closely related, yet, distinct factors. The applied potential can drive a reaction forward. Additionally, electric fields in the extended environment can modulate the ensembles that determine the activation parameters, without necessarily constituting a thermodynamic driving force themselves.

title: Discovery and development of antimicrobial polymers
abstract: Antimicrobial polymers offer an attractive tool for combating the crisis of antimicrobial resistance. This Review highlights recent advances in antimicrobial polymer development and discusses future directions, including the use of machine learning to guide polymer design and the development of scalable production methods to ensure global accessibility of these materials.

title: Reaction energy and spin density identify a compact physically interpretable descriptor set beyond the Bell-Evans-Polanyi relationship for hydrogen atom transfer
abstract: Although hydrogen atom transfer (HAT) reactions broadly follow the Bell-Evans-Polanyi (BEP) relationship, the physical origin of systematic deviations from this relationship remains insufficiently understood. Here, we combine high-level DLPNO-CCSD(T) barrier calculations for 400 HAT reactions and their reverse reactions with interpretable machine learning to identify a compact set of physically meaningful descriptors associated with activation barriers beyond reaction thermodynamics.

title: High-pressure behavior of the low-frequency mode of water
abstract: The low-frequency (LF) mode observed in the THz spectrum of liquid water near 10 meV has been known for decades, yet its microscopic origin remains debated. Leading interpretations assign it to a transverse acoustic-like excitation, a transverse optic-like mode, or a mode-mode coupling mechanism. We address this question by probing the collective dynamics of H$_2$O and D$_2$O at room temperature and pressures from 0.1 to 1 GPa using high-resolution (1.6 meV) inelastic X-ray scattering (IXS). The LF mode remains heavily damped, close to critical damping, throughout the explored range, while its frequency hardens markedly with pressure, much more than expected for a transverse acoustic mode. Comparison with IXS measurements and \textit{ab initio} simulations of crystalline Ice VI reveals a cluster of weakly dispersive modes in the same energy range, suggesting that the low-frequency mode in liquid water reflects a mixed character arising from the superposition of several branches rather than a single well-defined excitation, providing a coherent microscopic picture of water's anomalous THz dynamics under compression.

title: Speed-to-Power Dominates Energy Costs for AI Data Centers: Technoeconomic Analysis of Powering AI in the Continental United States
abstract: The rapid growth of artificial intelligence is driving demand for new data centers at large scale and on short deployment timelines. To power them, firms connect to the commercial grid or contract generation directly, but interconnection and gas-turbine delays now incentivize on-site generation. We compare grid-connected and off-grid data center energy infrastructure (AC- and DC-coupled solar-plus-storage, islanded natural gas, and grid interconnection) across the continental U.S. Using an open-source technoeconomic framework built on empirically calibrated AI training loads, climate-driven cooling, stage-by-stage power conversion, and physics-based battery degradation, we model designs providing equivalent energy services. Our central contribution is a speed-adjusted cost of energy that values the compute unlocked by faster construction, making options with different deployment timelines directly comparable on one physically consistent basis. We find DC coupling reduces lifetime energy costs by 18% ($0.09/ kWh) on average versus AC counterparts by eliminating inverters and improving efficiency. Though rarely cheapest on unadjusted energy cost, DC-coupled microgrids' faster deployment makes them the lowest-cost modeled option in 85% of U.S. locations once foregone compute is valued, or 55% under accelerated natural gas timelines. For AI infrastructure, deployment speed rather than unit energy cost determines the economically preferred path to power.

title: AI for Biologists: The Knowledge Boundaries of Foundation Models in the Age of Agentic Systems
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing how biological research is done. Biological foundation models trained on millions of nucleotides, protein, and single-cell measurements predict protein structures, mutation effects, and cellular responses to genetic perturbations. Agentic systems, AI assistants built on large language models, can run multistep analyses from plain-language requests and increasingly call foundation models as tools. Yet it is often unclear when these models' outputs can be trusted. We frame this as a model's knowledge boundary: the range of inputs, tasks, and conditions over which its outputs are reliable. This review explains how foundation models are built and proposes that five design elements (data, architecture, training scheme, evaluation scheme, and post-analysis) define this boundary. We examine evidence on where current models succeed or fail and present standardized descriptions of model limits so that researchers, and the agents acting for them, can use these tools reliably.

title: Brønsted Acid Site-Mediated Proton Injection and Redistribution Regulate Phosphoric Acid Electrochemical Interfaces
abstract: Molecular control of the proton environment in phosphoric acid (PA) based electrochemical interfaces is critical for efficient proton transport and oxygen reduction reaction (ORR), yet effective strategies for actively regulating this environment remain limited. Here, we show that Brønsted acid sites (BASs) in HY zeolite function as solid-state proton regulating centers that directly participate in and reorganize the interfacial PA hydrogen bond network.

title: Nonlinear Field-Reorganization Coupling Dictates Cation-Steered Proton Transfer at Electrified Interfaces
abstract: Electrolyte cations in the electric double layer strongly influence electrocatalytic CO2 reduction to multicarbon products, yet the microscopic origin of this cation effect remains elusive. Using metadynamics-biased ab initio molecular dynamics simulations, we identify a cation-driven electrostatic traction mechanism, where the cation-induced local electric field promotes the interfacial water activation and directly steers nascent protons toward adsorbed *CO2 via an Eley–Rideal path, effectively bypassing the Volmer H adsorption intermediate as the dominant channel under these interfacial…

title: Molecular Determinants of Contaminant Association with PET Nanoplastics Revealed by Atomistic Simulations
abstract: Chemical contaminants associated with nanoplastics can form environmentally pervasive, persistent complexes with potentially toxic effects. Yet, determining which contaminants are most likely to associate with nanoplastics and which molecular determinants govern this phenomenon remains challenging. Here, we used molecular dynamics (MD) to screen and compare the surface association of small-molecule contaminants with polyethylene terephthalate nanoplastic particles (PET-NPPs). Toward this aim, we developed an automated, open-source MD screening pipeline that requires only a SMILES string as input. By systematically analyzing 203 environmentally relevant contaminants in complex with a PET-NPP model, we observed widespread surface association governed by a specific set of physicochemical descriptors. Contaminant net charge defined the primary interaction regime. Among neutral contaminants, association increased strongly with molecular size at lower molecular weights. Among compounds of comparable size, the strongest binders were consistent with geometric complementarity with the PET surface, involving aromatic anchoring and, in some cases, conformational adaptability. Together, these results identify model-specific molecular determinants of contaminant association with PET-NPPs, providing a framework that enables rapid, internally consistent prioritization of contaminants for targeted experimental and mechanistic follow-up.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Explainable Deep Learning (DL) and GIS-Based Spatial Assessment of Urban River Water Quality
abstract: Rivers are essential freshwater resources; however, rapid urbanization, industrial discharge, and untreated municipal wastewater have significantly degraded river water quality in densely populated cities such as Dhaka, Bangladesh, threatening environmental sustainability and public health. This study aims to develop an interpretable Deep Learning (DL) and Geographic Information Systems (GIS) based framework for predicting the Water Quality Index (WQI) and identifying the dominant physicochemical and heavy metal parameters influencing water quality in the Turag, Balu, Shitalakshya, and…

title: Lipids from banana peels help cherry tomatoes stay fresh longer
abstract: Fruits and vegetables keep "breathing" even after they're picked. Respiration consumes sugars and organic acids that contribute to flavor, while moisture loss and continued ripening soften the fruit. These changes shorten shelf life and contribute to food waste. Thin edible coatings can be applied to regulate gas and water transfer and preserve fresh produce. Now, food scientists are exploring whether byproducts we often discard could supply ingredients for these coatings.

title: Multiscale computational modeling of circulating tumor cells: From separation and detection to targeted drug delivery.
abstract: Circulating tumor cells (CTCs) provide a minimally invasive window into cancer progression and metastatic dissemination; however, their extreme rarity, phenotypic heterogeneity, and mechanical adaptability make their isolation, identification, and therapeutic targeting challenging. Although computational methods have been applied to individual steps of CTC research, the field lacks a unified framework connecting molecular recognition, cell mechanics, microfluidic separation, detection, vascular transport, and targeted drug delivery.

title: Radical-Based Catalytic Transformations of 1-Azabicyclo[1.1.0]butanes: Opportunities and Future Directions
abstract: 1-Azabicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (ABBs) have emerged as versatile strained precursors to saturated, three-dimensional azetidine scaffolds that are increasingly valuable in modern drug discovery. This Perspective contends that the recent proliferation of radical-based catalytic platforms, encompassing photoredox, metallaphotoredox, energy-transfer, and electrochemical manifolds, serves as an effective complement to classical polar chemistry, enabling diverse transformations and the construction of sterically congested carbon–carbon and carbon–heteroatom bonds through distinct reactivity profiles.

title: New way of detecting date-rape drug use found in Switzerland
abstract: Swiss researchers have found a new way of detecting the notorious date-rape drug GHB in urine for up to 72 hours after ingestion, in a possible boon to sexual assault investigations.

title: Collapse of Li+ percolation networks in lithium-rich cathodes: origins, kinetics, and strategies for restoring fast lithium transport.
abstract: Lithium-rich layered oxide cathodes offer specific capacities exceeding 250 mAh g-1 through coupled cationic and anionic redox reactions, but poor rate capability, voltage fade, and structural degradation hinder their practical application. This review proposes the progressive collapse of Li+ percolation networks as a unifying, under-recognized transport bottleneck.

title: A dual locally active memristive Hopfield neural network: hidden dynamics and multistability for medical image encryption
abstract: The increasing demand for secure medical image transmission exposes limitations of conventional encryption. This work presents a two-memristor Hopfield neural network (2 M-HNN) incorporating two locally active memristors: a multi-equilibrium-state memristor with trigonometric-polynomial hybrid memductance and Gaussian-localized flux perturbation, emulating electromagnetic irradiation, and a Gaussian-envelope rational memristor with sech2 damping, replicating autaptic synaptic feedback.

title: FamGeo-DDG: A Mutation-Centered Local Geometric-Semantic Framework for Protein–Protein ΔΔ G Prediction
abstract: Protein–protein interactions (PPIs) are central to cellular regulation, immune recognition, and therapeutic design, making accurate prediction of mutation-induced binding free energy changes (ΔΔG) important for variant interpretation and protein engineering. However, ΔΔG prediction remains challenging because mutational effects are often localized, while benchmark performance may be inflated by residual similarity between training and validation complexes. Here, we present FamGeo-DDG, a mutation-centered local geometric-semantic framework for protein–protein ΔΔG prediction.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: White wine drinkers help pinpoint what's missing in no- and low-alcohol drinks
abstract: Researchers at The University of Queensland are on a quest to identify key aroma compounds that could make no- and low-alcohol (NOLO) wine more attractive to drinkers.

title: CT-based machine learning and multimodal prediction in acute pancreatitis: a narrative review.
abstract: Acute pancreatitis (AP) has a highly variable clinical course. This narrative review focuses on computed tomography (CT) radiomics, deep learning and clinical-imaging models for severity and adverse-outcome prediction, with clinical-only models as context. A targeted PubMed search checked on 16 October 2026, with a publication cutoff of 14 October 2026, retrieved 80 unique records; ten CT-informed exemplars and eight clinical-context studies were selected for detailed comparison. This is a representative, non-exhaustive synthesis.

title: Light-Driven Reconstruction of MoS2 Nanosheets Boosts Photothermal Reverse Water Gas Shift Reaction with Near-Unity Selectivity
abstract: In-depth understanding of the reconstruction behaviors during photothermal reactions is of paramount importance for the design of highly efficient photothermal catalysts. Here, we demonstrate the photothermal effect-induced reconstruction of MoS2 nanosheets during the photothermal reverse water gas shift (RWGS) reaction. Specifically, under the operating photothermal reaction conditions, the MoS2 nanosheet catalyst undergoes rapid surface temperature increase up to around 380 °C, which can react with the H2 gas to produce in-plane S vacancies, thereby leading to the reconstruction of MoS2…

title: Vacancy-Directed Phytate Coordination Couples Ni-Site Polarization with Interfacial Hydration for Durable Photoelectrochemical Seawater Oxidation
abstract: Photoelectrochemical seawater oxidation is limited by a coupled interfacial challenge: low-coordinated metal sites that favor hole utilization and oxygen evolution are also susceptible to chloride attack, whereas protective surface modification can compromise water access. Here, oxygen vacancies in amorphous NiCr2O4–x on α-Fe2O3 are repurposed to direct multidentate phytate coordination, constructing a molecular interface that couples Ni-site polarization with interfacial hydration.

title: Developmental Differences in Gamma-Band Brain Connectivity During Propofol and Sevoflurane Anesthesia in Children
abstract: Background Propofol and sevoflurane are commonly used pediatric anesthetics with distinct molecular targets; however, their differential modulation of developing brain networks across age groups remains poorly understood. Unlike scalp low-frequency EEG, source-space gamma-band functional connectivity reflects cortical processing and may offer a sensitive window into drug-specific effects.
