This study aimed to identify distinct gamma-band connectivity patterns distinguishing propofol from sevoflurane anesthesia using explainable machine learning.

title: A Multimetallic Single-Atom Catalyst on a Defective Graphene Support toward Methanol Oxidation and Oxygen Reduction Reactions: Density Functional Theory, Machine Learning, and Experiments.
abstract: Multimetallic single-atom catalysts (SACs) have emerged as promising candidates for electrocatalytic reactions. However, identifying bifunctional multimetallic SACs capable of efficiently catalyzing both the oxygen reduction and methanol oxidation reactions (ORR and MOR), applicable to direct methanol fuel cells, remains challenging due to the vast compositional design space. Here, we propose a defective graphene-supported multimetallic SAC (M1M2M3M4M5-SAC) incorporating Mn, Pt, Fe, Ni, Co, and Cu for simultaneous MOR and ORR catalysis.

title: Hybrid Weakly Coordinated Solvents for Fast-Charging and Wide-Temperature Sodium-Ion Full Batteries
abstract: The application of sodium-ion batteries (SIBs) in wide-temperature and fast-charging scenarios is severely constrained by the performance limitations of electrolytes. Conventional ester-based electrolytes struggle to simultaneously achieve high ionic conductivity, low desolvation energy, and excellent interfacial stability. Herein, we propose a hybrid solvent system comprising ethyl propionate and ethoxy(pentafluoro)cyclotriphosphazene (PFPN), aiming to synergistically enhance the rate capability and temperature adaptability of SIBs.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Torque generation and regulation in the flagellar motor of Campylobacter jejuni differ from those of model organisms
abstract: The bacterial flagellar motor is a rotary nanomachine that powers motility by driving the rotation of a helical filament. Most of our mechanistic understanding of this motor derives from studies of model organisms, particularly Escherichia coli and Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium, yet recent structural work has revealed substantial architectural diversity, raising questions about the universality of established biophysical models. Here, we present the first single-motor measurements of torque output and stator dynamics in Campylobacter jejuni, a species with a structurally elaborate motor adapted for motility in high-viscosity environments. The C.~jejuni motor generates an exceptionally high stall torque (~3600~pN{middle dot}nm) and, rather than the biphasic torque--speed relationship characteristic of model systems, exhibits an approximately linear decline in torque with increasing speed over the measured range. Time-resolved measurements reveal discrete speed changes, indicating that the stator output remains dynamic despite the presence of a scaffolded stator ring. The inferred number of active stator units averaged 11{+/-}4, below the 17-unit complement observed structurally, and showed no clear dependence on viscous load despite substantial motor-to-motor heterogeneity. Following transient collapse of the proton motive force, motor activity recovers rapidly, consistent with reversible activation of pre-associated stator units. Together, these findings reveal a distinct mode of flagellar motor operation, consistent with dynamic regulation of a preassembled stator ring rather than regulation through physical stator exchange, and show that the canonical behavior defined in model organisms is not universal.

title: PIANO enables generative modeling of gene expression and scales multi-omics integration to 100 million cells
abstract: Single-cell RNA technologies enable the routine acquisition of transcriptomic atlases. However, these molecular profiles are influenced by overlapping sources of variation. Since these covariates confound comparisons, data integration is the first step in most analyses. Three challenges remain: correcting strong batch effects, scaling to millions of cells, and modeling how covariates influence gene expression. To address these challenges, we developed PIANO, probabilistic inference autoencoder networks for multi-omics, a deep learning framework whose central feature is a generative model of gene expression data. Additionally, PIANO achieves robust integrations and trains 10× faster than previous methods. PIANO accurately integrates single-cell data across species and across single-cell and spatial transcriptomics modalities. As practical applications, PIANO models spatially resolved gene expression during Alzheimer's disease progression in human brains and integrates over 100 million cancer cells to model drug perturbations. In summary, PIANO's integration and generative modeling capabilities will empower novel insights for a wide range of future studies.

title: Pallatom2: Navigating the De Novo Protein Universe with Atom-to-Atom Modeling
abstract: Protein binder design requires precise coordination of molecular structure, binding geometry, and experimentally measurable performance. We introduce Pallatom2, an efficient, precise Atom-to-Atom generative model that jointly models protein sequence, backbone conformation, side-chain geometry, and target-interface contacts. A unified Atom14 representation and residue-guided sparse all-atom attention enable bidirectional information exchange between residue-level and atom-level representations, coordinating global structure with local atomic detail in a compact model of just 65.9 million…

title: A Three-Gene Panel with Prognostic Potential Identified by WGCNA and Machine Learning in Acute Myeloid Leukemia: Evidence from RT-qPCR Validation
abstract: Background Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) represents the most prevalent form of leukemia in adults, arising from the accumulation of multiple genetic mutations and dysregulated gene expression. The substantial molecular heterogeneity characteristic of AML contributes to variability in treatment responses, underscoring the critical importance of understanding the prognostic implications of genetic alterations for guiding therapeutic decisions. Therefore, this study aimed to identify novel genes with prognostic potential in AML patients.

title: CPPainter: Painting Cell-Penetrating Peptides for Identification and Generation through Reinforcement Learning
abstract: Cell-penetrating peptides (CPPs) are promising intracellular delivery vectors, but computational CPP identification, sequence optimization, and candidate generation are often studied as separate tasks. This study aimed to develop an integrated framework for CPP prediction and reward-guided sequence design. We developed CPPainter, a computational framework that couples a protein language model ensemble classifier with a reinforcement-learning-guided generator. CPPainter-Classifier outputs a continuous CPP probability score for CPP identification and sequence-level reward assignment.
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Catalyst regeneration enables durable hydrogen production from ammonia
abstract: Researchers at the National University of Singapore (NUS) have developed a catalyst-regeneration strategy that could make hydrogen production from ammonia more efficient and reliable. By tackling a major problem that causes catalysts to lose their effectiveness over time, the team sustained hydrogen production for over 2,000 hours in laboratory tests.

title: Identifying crosstalk genes between bipolar disorder and osteoporosis via machine learning and experimental validation.
abstract: Bipolar disorder (BD) has been recognized as an independent risk factor for osteoporosis (OP), yet the shared genetic and molecular mechanisms underlying their comorbidity remain largely unexplored. This study aimed to identify potential crosstalk genes between BD and OP using bioinformatics and machine learning, and to validate their expression patterns in an established in vitro osteoporotic cell model.
venue: Journal of pharmacological and toxicological methods

title: Schatten-p and HSIC-Guided Tensor Subspace Clustering with Dual Noise and Sparse Gradients for Multi-Omics Cancer Subtyping.
abstract: Cancer multi-omics data can characterize tumor heterogeneity from different molecular levels and provide an important information source for unsupervised cancer subtype discovery. However, existing tensorized multi-view subspace clustering methods still face problems in practical cancer sub typing tasks, including insufficiently compact tensor low-rank approximation, noise modeling limited to a single space, overly rigid constraints on cross-view relationships, and insufficient preservation of local boundary structures in the affinity matrix.
venue: IEEE transactions on computational biology and bioinformatics

title: Interfacial Confinement Enables Conformal IrOx Nanofilms for Low-Ir-Loading PEM Water Electrolysis
abstract: Terawatt-scale deployment of proton-exchange membrane water electrolyzers (PEMWEs) requires low iridium (Ir) loading, which disrupts the catalyst layer’s in-plane electronic percolation network and severely degrades performance. Here, we overcome this bottleneck via an interfacial confinement strategy that electrostatically enriches cationic Ir intermediates on the negatively charged, oxygen-deficient TiOx surface, thereby redirecting Ir deposition from three-dimensional island growth to a two-dimensional conformal film on TiO2 supports.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Breaking the “Micro-Size Inversion” Paradox via a Surface-Chemistry-Driven Molecular Sieving Membrane for Ambient Lithium–Air Batteries
abstract: Lithium–air batteries suffer from moisture-induced parasitic reactions and electrolyte evaporation in ambient air. A fundamental challenge is the “micro-size inversion” paradox, where H2O (0.275 nm) is smaller than O2 (0.346 nm), rendering conventional size-based sieving ineffective. Here, we report a composite membrane composed of polydimethylsiloxane and fluorinated vinyl-functionalized covalent organic framework (COF-VF) to break this selectivity barrier.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Streamlining Lateral Flow Assay (LFA) Data Analysis: A MATLAB® Live Script for Integrated Batch Image Processing and Limit of Detection Determination
abstract: Manual quantitative lateral flow assay (LFA) analysis can span at least three software environments: image-analysis software such as ImageJ, spreadsheets such as Excel, and coding tools using MATLAB, Python or R. Repeatedly defining Test, Control and background regions of interest (ROIs) for individual strips, transferring measurements and performing separate statistical and calibration analyses makes data analysis for standard-curve experiments laborious and introduces opportunities for manual handling errors.

title: Mesoporous curvature-induced proton coupled electron transfer for rapid photoredox of CO2 to CH4
abstract: The photoreduction of CO 2 is usually terminated by two-electron processes resulting in predominantly products CO, the formulation of eight-electron products CH 4 still remains a great challenge limited by proton coupled electron transfer (PCET) abilities. Here, a novel type of two-dimensional (2-D) mesoporous TiO 2 (mTiO 2 ) has been synthesized based on the nanoscale titanium-oxo cluster units for rapid photoredox of CO 2 to CH 4 . In this unique 2-D structure, a mesoporous sheet with ~ 2.7 nm in thickness and several micrometers in size, can be stably formed into uniform hexagonal arrays.

title: Water efficient anion receptors based on naphthalene self-association
abstract: New water-soluble molecular receptors for carboxylates and phenylphosphonates with a pseudo-macrocyclic structure are reported. Distinct from traditional macrocyclic covalent scaffolds, these linear receptors create a cavity upon supramolecular pi-pi association between two naphthalene rings, which is strengthen in aqueous solution. Notably, this strategy allows a fast, high yield, easy to scale-up synthesis compared to macrocyclic preparation.

title: Direct catalytic formation of styrene from acetylene
abstract: Direct synthesis of styrene from simple C2 feedstocks remains unrealized, reflecting the strong thermodynamic bias of acetylene towards cyclotrimerization to benzene. Such a process would circumvent currently employed energy-intensive routes to styrene, which today is produced on a >30 Mt scale annually. Here, we report unification of acetylene cyclotrimerization and alkyne hydroarylation in the direct conversion of acetylene to styrene at a single earth-abundant metal centre.

title: Stability of hydroxide-like intermediates in hydrated models of creatine dehydration
abstract: We tested whether C–O cleavage during creatine dehydration can precede proton transfer in clusters containing six explicit waters. For one Ca2+ hydration arrangement, an intrinsic reaction coordinate traced at GFN2-xTB connected the neighborhoods of hydroxide-like and water-bearing minima. The C–O distance remained above 2.70 Å throughout the trace. Two hydroxide-like geometries gave local minima after reoptimization in both ALPB and GBSA water. At PBE/def2-SVP with CPCM water, the original hydroxide-like geometry relaxed to a water-bearing structure.

title: Unveiling the photophysics of α-substituted amino BODIPYs
abstract: Upon proper functionalization, BODIPY dyes can be employed as fluorescent probes or singlet oxygen photosensitizers. Despite the number of photophysical studies on these systems, clear structural-photophysical guidelines for the rational design of BODIPY derivatives for a particular purpose are still scarce. In this study we have employed the second order algebraic diagrammatic construction, ADC(2) method to investigate the impact of the second a substituent on the photophysics of three a-amino substituted BODIPY dyes.

title: Photophysical insights on the phototoxicity of p -aminobenzoic acid
abstract: P -aminobenzoic acid (PABA) is known to induce photosensitised reactions in the DNA. In this contribution we provide static multirreference (XMS-CASPT2) insight on the probable deactivation mechanism behind these reactions. PABA is excited by UV-B radiation, which populates the bright second electronically excited state. Relaxation leads readily to the S 1 potential, where we found two minima of different character (ππ ∗ and nπ ∗ ). Ground state recovery via internal conversions within the singlet potentials is unlikely, thus confirming a triplet-mediated deactivation.

title: Computational Insights into Alizarin’s Suitability for Advanced Solar Energy Technologies
abstract: Understanding the photophysical properties of molecular dyes is essential for exploring their potential applications in solar energy conversion and storage. In this work, we investigate the excited-state behavior of alizarin and its potential applications in dyesensitized solar cells (DSSCs) and molecular solar thermal (MOST) systems. Using TD-DFT, MS-CASPT2, and MR-SF-TD-DFT calculations, we characterize its absorption and emission spectra and explore the ground-and excited-state potential energy surfaces.

title: A Critical Analysis of Spontaneous Hydrogen Peroxide (H2O2) Formation at the Air–Water Interface: Reconciling Conflicting Reports
abstract: Recent reports of spontaneous hydrogen peroxide (H2O2) formation in microdroplets have sparked productive debate, with mechanisms falling into two families: those invoking the air–water interface – (i) ultrahigh electric fields driving the formation of HO• from HO−, (ii) comproportionation of water into H2O•+ and H2O•−, and (iii) partial dehydration of interfacial H+ and HO− – and those invoking other pathways, namely (iv) O2 reduction at water–solid contacts, (v) sonochemistry, and (vi) tribochemistry.

title: Proteins as Hierarchies of Modules: Exact Elastic-Network Thermodynamics of Folding and Function
abstract: Lattice models suggested information-theoretic rules for protein foldability and function but cannot represent the architecture of real proteins. Using Gaussian and anisotropic elastic network models of 183 globular proteins and 77 functional systems, an Ising–Gaussian network model of folding in which every native-contact state carries its exact chain entropy, and statistical mechanics, information theory and variational autoencoders, we show that native proteins are hierarchies of modules.

title: Water-Mediated Electrochemical Oxidative Dearomatization of Indoles: A Sustainable Approach to 2-Hydroxyindolin-3-ones
abstract: A mild, green and metal-free electrochemical oxidative dearomatization process to achieve 2-hydroxy-2-phenyloxindolin-3-ones bearing a C2-quaternary centre has been established from mono-substituted or disubstituted indoles. In this transformation, water serves as both a hydroxyl and an oxygen source, enabling the formation of C2-hydroxyl and C3-carbonyl functionalities. The protocol accommodated a broad range of substrates, affording the desired products in moderate to good yields.

title: Ligand Rollover C-H Activation as a Strategy for Intermolecular C-H Activation
abstract: The thermolysis of ( N NNN O )Pt II (CH 3 ) ( 1 ) (H- N NNN O = 2-[5-( tert- butyl)-3-isoxazolyl]-6-[5-( tert -butyl)-1H-pyrazol-3-yl]pyridine) in C 6 D 6 at 100 °C produced methane- h 4 and ( N NNN O - d 1 )Pt II (C 6 D 5 ) ( 2-D ) with a deuterated isoxazolyl group, consistent with a mechanism involving ligand rollover C-H activation. Ligand rollover-mediated intramolecular hydrocarbon activation represents a new metal-ligand-cooperative strategy for application in hydrocarbon functionalization.

title: Fine-Tuning Locally Deployable Scientific Language Models: Reliability and Resource Tradeoffs
abstract: Commercial cloud-based language models increasingly support scientific research, but transmitting unpublished data raises concerns about privacy and institutional control. Small, locally deployable open-weight models offer an alternative, yet whether domain fine-tuning improves scientific reliability enough to justify its resource costs remains uncertain. Using electrochemistry as a test domain, we converted 4,983 open-access papers into 86,329 questionanswer pairs and fine-tuned eleven models (3-32 billion parameters) using low-rank adaptation.

title: Activity–dissolution trade-offs in multicomponent electrocatalysts
abstract: Electrocatalyst development has largely focused on improving catalytic activity, while the loss of valuable metals through electrochemical dissolution has received comparatively little attention. Yet, minimizing material loss is essential for the resource-efficient use of scarce metals in energy-conversion technologies. Here we introduce activity–dissolution trade-off mapping as a framework for integrating catalytic performance and material retention into catalyst design.

title: DFTB Parameterization Framework for Actinide Molten Salts: Multivalent U–Cl Fuel Salt Parameters
abstract: Actinide fuel salts are a crucial part of the molten salt reactors. However, the chemistry of these salts under high temperature environments are under explored as complex electronic structure of actinides make it quite difficult to study the evolution of their molten structure for long timescale at Density Functional theory level. Semi-empirical methods such as Density Functional Tight Binding (DFTB) exist which can probe the underlying chemistry with long timescale dynamics but it lacks the required parameters.

title: Effects of Hyperthermal Atomic Oxygen and Surface Topology on Germanium Coatings Used to Reduce Drag in Low Earth Orbit
abstract: Low-altitude orbit spacecraft require materials that resist hyperthermal atomic oxygen (AO) erosion and maintain low-drag gas-surface interactions. In this work, we examine thin germanium (Ge) coatings as a non-native oxide-forming surface that generate a protective oxide layer in situ under AO exposure while preserving favorable scattering behavior. Ge-coated silicon samples are exposed to a hyperthermal O/O2 beam representative of low Earth orbit conditions and are analyzed using mass-loss measurements, atomic force microscopy (AFM), X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS), molecular-beam…

title: C2 Substitution Controls Charge-Transfer Dynamics and Suppresses Triplet Population in Barbituric Acid Push–Pull Chromophores
abstract: Barbituric acid derivatives are structurally versatile chromophores with emerging utility in biological and optical applications. In this study, the photophysical properties of two conjugated barbituric acid-based push-pull systems, BAO2 and its thionated analogue BAS2, are investigated to elucidate how oxygen-to-sulfur substitution at the C2 position controls excited-state behavior. Both molecules feature an electron-donating aromatic unit covalently linked to an electron-accepting barbituric acid core through a π-conjugated bridge, promoting strong intramolecular charge transfer.

title: Azetidine-Driven SuFEx Macrocyclization and Bioconjugation
abstract: Chemoselective macrocyclization of unprotected peptides in aqueous media is essential for generating large screening libraries and advancing hit compounds toward therapeutic candidates; however, developing a broadly applicable strategy remains challenged by incomplete conversion, cross-reactivity with proteogenic side chains, and linker instability. Here, we report an azetidinedriven sulfur(VI) fluoride exchange (AzetSuFEx) platform to address these bottlenecks.

title: Certified distance of two-body reduced density matrices to the ensemble N-representable set
abstract: Variational two-electron reduced density matrix (2-RDM) methods give accurate energies, but their 2-RDMs need not correspond to any N-electron wave function; recent variational quantum algorithms proposed the distance of a 2-RDM to the set of such physical (N-representable) 2-RDMs as a Hamiltonian-independent measure of its quality and estimated it from above for systems of up to four spatial orbitals.

title: Localized Electrochemical Writing and Readout of Polyoxovanadate Charge States in Confined Microdroplets
abstract: Redox-active molecules are promising building blocks for programmable charge states in molecular-scale information storage, but practical implementation requires precise control over redox behavior within complex local chemical environments. Here, we demonstrate that scanning electrochemical cell microscopy (SECCM) can be used to prepare spatially resolved programmed patterns on surfaces by molecular charge storage with carboxyl-functionalized vanadium polyoxometalates (POMs), and subsequently use SECCM for readout of the stored charges.

title: Closed-Loop Bayesian Optimization for the Synthesis of Amine-Grafted Resins for Direct Air Capture
abstract: Direct air capture (DAC) of CO 2 requires adsorbents that combine high uptake with fast adsorption kinetics, yet whether these properties can be co-optimized remains unresolved. Here we couple automated high-throughput synthesis and characterization of amine-grafted porous polymers with multi-objective Bayesian optimization in a closed loop. Jointly optimizing equilibrium CO 2 uptake and adsorption rate at 400 ppm CO 2 , we discover a kinetics-uptake trade-off described by a linear Pareto curve, uncovering adsorbents with order-of-magnitude higher adsorption kinetics than benchmark adsorbents…

title: Functional Specialization of Coordination Spheres Enables Site-Selective Aromatic C–H Isotope Exchange in Ni Single-Atom Catalysts
abstract: Engineering single-atom catalysts has predominantly focused on tailoring the primary coordination sphere, whereas whether distinct coordination spheres can be endowed with independent catalytic functions remains largely unexplored. Here, we demonstrate the functional specialization of coordination spheres by constructing a phosphorus-modified Ni–N2O2 single-atom catalyst for site-selective C–H deuteration.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Lemon waste yields bioplastic more flexible than commercial counterpart, study finds
abstract: A new research article published in Polymers explores an innovative way to turn lemon processing residues into biopolymers. Authored by ANIPH's coordinator, CETEC, together with partners from companion projects Viss and PHAntastic, the study investigated the use of lemon industry byproducts as carbon sources for PHBV production using the halophilic archaeon Haloferax mediterranei.

title: Linker Steric Hindrance-Induced Defect Engineering Enables Oxygen Vacancy-Rich MOFs for Pollutant Degradation
abstract: The widespread contamination of water by emerging contaminants (ECs) demands the development of efficient remediation technologies. Although advanced oxidation processes reliant on reactive oxygen species (ROS) show promise, they typically depend on energy- or reagent-intensive activation methods. Here, we introduce a linker steric hindrance-induced defect engineering (LSH-DE) strategy for metal–organic frameworks, which enables catalytic ROS generation using molecular oxygen (O2) as a benign terminal oxidant at ambient temperature and pressure.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Mapping the Slow Propagation of Disorder across a Photoreceptor’s Tertiary Structure with Time-Resolved Crystallography
abstract: Order–disorder transitions allow many proteins to shift between compact and flexible/unfolded states, thereby acting as structural switches that regulate catalysis, signaling, recognition, and allostery. We applied time-resolved serial oscillation crystallography to establish the structural kinetics of the light-triggered order–disorder transition of an animal-like cryptochrome as a six-second-long molecular movie with near-atomic all-residue spatial resolution and millisecond temporal resolution. Our 29 structural snapshots mapped the propagation of disorder across the tertiary structure motifs of a cryptochrome’s C-terminal region, triggered by a single broken D321–R492 salt bridge. The order–disorder transition followed a nucleation-propagation mechanism reminiscent of helix–coil dynamics and proceeded over up to five seconds, with regions distal to the D321–R492 trigger initially undergoing slow zero-order disordering before switching to first-order unfolding kinetics. Our per-residue density analysis provides a detailed structural-kinetic basis for understanding how order–disorder transitions emerge through directional propagation across protein tertiary structures, as occurring in signaling and many other biological systems.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Research progress in the photocatalytic reduction of carbon dioxide over nitride catalysts: a review.
abstract: Photocatalytic CO2 emission reduction uses solar energy to convert the greenhouse gas CO2 into fuel and high-value-added carbon-based chemicals. Nitride materials with tunable electronic structures, rich nitrogen-containing active sites, excellent visible light responsiveness and chemical stability have become a class of promising new photocatalytic systems. In this paper, the research progress of nitride catalysts in the field of photocatalytic CO2 reduction is reviewed, and the basic mechanism and a recommended framework for evaluating photocatalytic CO2 reduction are expounded.

title: Reverse Water Gas Shift Reaction over a Homogeneous Iron Catalyst and the Underlying Mechanism
abstract: The CO production by the reverse water gas shift (RWGS) reaction is a promising bridge between CO2 conversion and well-established C1 chemistry. Currently, heterogeneous catalysts are mostly reported for this reaction, which usually require high operating temperatures (above 600 °C) and encounter poor selectivity of CO at lower temperatures (below 400 °C). Homogeneous catalysis may offer distinct advantages at a low temperature. Nevertheless, only some noble metal homogeneous catalysts for this reaction have been reported to date.

title: Divergent Proteomic Responses to Lead Exposure in House Sparrows (Passer domesticus)
abstract: Chronic exposure to environmental contaminants can drive population decline but also exert selective pressure favouring adaptive molecular responses that mitigate toxicity. Australian lead (Pb) mining and smelting towns provide a natural experiment to study such contemporary adaptation in the house sparrow (Passer domesticus), an invasive commensal species that has persisted in heavily contaminated environments for over a century. The Broken Hill population is of particular interest as it has remained geographically isolated with limited gene flow, whereas the Port Pirie population is connected to surrounding regions. Here, we used data-independent acquisition mass spectrometry to compare the blood and liver proteomes of wild-caught sparrows from both towns and identify divergent molecular responses to lead. Lead exposure altered the mitochondrial proteome and disrupted RNA splicing in both populations, but the two towns diverged sharply in haem biosynthesis and protein quality control. We identified a mechanistic cascade in which lead inhibits ALAD, depleting intracellular haem, stabilising the transcriptional repressor BACH1, and suppressing globin expression. Broken Hill birds maintained ALAD abundance, upregulated proteasomal subunits (PSMC) and HSP70 family chaperones, and preserved significantly higher haemoglobin concentrations despite equivalent blood lead levels. Port Pirie birds exhibited ALAD collapse, BACH1 accumulation, and reliance on autophagy rather than active protein quality control. Liver proteomics confirmed tissue-level convergence of the haem pathway disruption. Together, these findings reveal that over a century of isolation under sustained lead exposure has shaped population-specific molecular strategies in Broken Hill sparrows, with enhanced proteostasis and preserved haem biosynthesis representing signatures of local adaptation.

title: Multimodal protein representations across human brain cell types
abstract: The central nervous system (CNS) comprises diverse cell types whose molecular context shapes the roles of the proteins they express. Computational models offer a scalable way to study the roles of proteins across human brain cell types, with protein language models and interactome- or single-cell-based models capturing complementary information encoded in protein sequences and cellular network contexts. Human brain tissue is hard to access, so brain cell types make up a small fraction of the atlases single-cell models train on and of the benchmarks used for their evaluation.

title: Specific Amino Acid Imaging of Protein Condensates in Live Cells by Stimulated Raman Scattering Microscopy
abstract: Intracellular protein condensates formed by liquid–liquid phase separation have gained increasing attention in recent years due to their key roles in many physiological and pathological processes. However, fluorescence imaging of protein condensates is limited by the bulky fluorescent tags that could perturb the protein localization and interaction. Imaging techniques that can visualize protein condensates in live cells with minimal perturbations remain lacking.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Modular Synthesis of α-Tertiary Amines Enabled by Nickel-Catalyzed Reductive Alkylation of N -unprotected Ketimines
abstract: The straightforward construction of sterically hindered α-tertiary primary amines remains a stubborn challenge in organic synthesis. Although a wide array of approaches for the synthesis of this motif has been developed, the leveraging of ketimines as an amine source is underexplored. General reductive alkylative additions of unactivated alkyl halides to N-unprotected ketimines remain unknown.

title: Thermodynamic analysis of electroosmotic transport in a williamson ternary nanofluid over a riga surface with coupled heat and reactive mass transfer
abstract: Accurate prediction of coupled momentum, heat, and mass transport in chemically reactive electrokinetic systems is important for the design of microscale thermal and electrochemical technologies. This study investigates the coupled transport characteristics of a Williamson ternary nanofluid over a Riga surface embedded in a Darcy-Forchheimer porous medium, incorporating electroosmotic effects, nonlinear thermal radiation, volumetric heat generation, homogeneous chemical reaction, and pollutant transport. The resulting nonlinear similarity equations are solved using MATLAB bvp4c solver, and a Bayesian-regularized artificial neural network (BR-ANN) is employed as a surrogate model for predicting principal transport quantities. The results reveal that electroosmotic forcing and electromagnetic actuation significantly enhance momentum, heat, and mass transport, whereas Darcy-Forchheimer resistance suppresses fluid motion. Nonlinear thermal radiation and volumetric heat generation increase thermal field, while homogeneous chemical reaction substantially alters concentration distribution and associated mass-transfer characteristics. Increasing ternary nanoparticle volume fraction to 3% produces marked enhancements in the transport performance, with skin-friction coefficient, Nusselt number, and Sherwood number increasing by 215.56%, 75.13%, and 10.77%, respectively. These results demonstrate the pronounced influence of ternary nanoparticle loading on momentum, heat, and mass transfer in the coupled electrokinetic system. Furthermore, the BR-ANN exhibits excellent predictive capability, achieving a correlation coefficient of R = 0.99999, with mean squared errors ranging from 10⁻⁷ to 10⁻¹⁰ for the predicted transport quantities. The combined numerical-ANN framework provides a reliable and computationally efficient approach for analyzing and optimizing chemically reactive electrokinetic nanofluid systems with potential applications in microreactors, electrochemical devices, catalytic microfluidic systems, lab-on-a-chip technologies, and microscale thermal management.

title: Experimental redox tuning of designed ferredoxins through sulfur to selenium substitutions
abstract: Iron–sulfur (Fe–S) clusters are essential for electron transfer in biology, and their redox potentials are finely tuned by both first-sphere ligation and the surrounding peptide environment. Here, we investigate both how minimal peptide scaffolds control cluster redox properties and how chalcogen substitution modulates these effects. Two designed peptides, corresponding to 28 residues of a bacterial ferredoxin-like sequence were assembled with both [4Fe–4S] and [4Fe–4Se] clusters, allowing a direct comparison of sulfur-to-selenium substitution within identical scaffolds.

title: Development of an Anionic Multicomponent Reaction for Rapid Construction of Highly Functionalized Dearomatized Scaffolds
abstract: Biosynthetic dearomatization of 3,5-dimethyl orsellinic acid (DMOA) affords highly functionalized cyclohexadienone precursors for enzymatic polyene cyclization to produce numerous complex meroterpenoids. In particular, dearomatized scaffolds derived from 2,4-dihydroxyl-3,5-dimethylphathalide (DHDMP) are valuable synthons for synthetic access to meroterpenoids.

title: Automated flow microscale synthesis of gamma-modified PNA unveils structural determinants of RNA hybridization
abstract: Peptide nucleic acids (PNA) are synthetic nucleic acid mimics in which the negatively charged sugar-phosphate backbone of DNA and RNA is replaced by a neutral pseudopeptide backbone. This neutral backbone reduces dependence on ionic strength, provides resistance to protease and nuclease degradation, and promotes high-affinity binding to complementary nucleic acids. Modification at the γ-carbon of the backbone can further improve solubility, reduce aggregation, and preorganize the backbone into a chiral helical conformation.

title: eRoboChem: Autonomous Electrosynthesis Across Redox Modes and Reactor Designs
abstract: Synthetic electrochemistry offers powerful opportunities for molecular synthesis, yet its broader adoption remains hindered by the complexity of electrochemical reaction development. Beyond conventional reaction parameters, electrosynthesis requires careful choice of electrode materials, reactor designs and control of electron transfer, creating a complex experimental and optimisation challenge that can deter many synthetic chemists.

title: From prototyping to daily practice: Chemically resistant 3D printed flow reactors for organic synthesis
abstract: The widespread adoption of flow chemistry in research remains limited by the cost and availability of suitable reactor equipment. 3D-printed (3DP) reactors could bridge this gap, but their adoption is limited because the thermal and chemical resistance of the printing materials are not yet fully understood. In this study, we establish an experimentally validated material selection platform that enables the selection and use of low-cost heat- and chemically resistant 3DP flow reactors in a wide range of synthetic applications.

title: Electrochemical Gas Bubble Production Drives Mass Transport Enhanced Destruction of Short Chain PFAS
abstract: Short chain perfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) (C4 to C6), exemplified herein by the C4 molecule perfluorobutanoic acid (PFBA), are considered harder to destroy than long chain PFAS. Herein, we report the use of an electrochemical flow cell containing two vertically orientated free-standing boron doped diamond (BDD) electrodes in a recirculating flow cell, treating solution volumes of 0.5 L. The cell is designed such 2 that recirculation flow zones (vortices) within the cell chamber are encouraged.

title: Intrinsically Safe Olefin Hydrogenation Catalysts
abstract: For exothermic reactions, such as olefin hydrogenation, the exponential rise in reaction rates with increasing temperature constitutes a safety hazard for large-scale reactions. Smart catalysts that switch themselves off when a reactor has become too hot could prevent accidents caused by thermal runaway. Here we report heterogeneous olefin hydrogenation catalysts that achieve turnover numbers exceeding 30,000 at 50 °C, but which reversibly switch themselves off at 120 °C.

title: H 2 O 2 -assisted vanadium catalysts on siliceous materials: support impact and V structure dynamics in CO 2 -promoted propane dehydrogenation
abstract: V-containing catalysts supported on purely siliceous materials are widely investigated for CO 2 -assisted propane dehydrogenation (CO 2 -PDH); however, the role of support properties in controlling the complex VOx speciation and its dynamic evolution under reaction conditions remains poorly understood. Here, we report a simple yet unconventional H 2 O 2 -assisted synthesis using V 2 O 5 to prepare V catalysts supported on fumed silica, MCM-41, and Silicalite-1.

title: Late Fluorescence Goes First: Dose-Resolved Suppression in Time-Gated Raman Spectroscopy of Recycled Poly(ethylene terephthalate)
abstract: The fluorescence of recycled poly(ethylene terephthalate) (rPET) was followed at two fixed spots with a time-gated Raman spectrometer (532 nm, 150 ps, 150 kHz), with the dose counted in laser pulses. At one spot, with the pile-up correction applied by the instrument software, the mean of the last three spectra, after 8.86 × 10 7 pulses, retained 0.208 ± 0.008 of the time-integrated fluorescence of the first run and 0.243 ± 0.009 of the gated fluorescence, and the Raman-to-fluorescence ratio increased by a factor of 5.52 ± 0.21 in the time-integrated data but by 4.87 ± 0.19 in the gated data.

title: Decoding Local Structural Changes in α-V2O5 Cathodes Associated with Mg-ion Batteries
abstract: Magnesium metal batteries promise higher energy density than lithium-ion systems, but their practical applicability is limited by the fact that cathode materials require elevated temperatures to achieve high reversible capacity at high potential. While the fundamental origin of this limitation remains unknown, the large potential hysteresis observed during cycling is a fingerprint of energyinefficient structural transformations that have never been resolved across both local and average length scales simultaneously.

title: On the role of boron in the direct dehydration of 1,3-butanediol into butadiene over Al,B-MFI catalysts
abstract: Direct dehydration of biomass-derived 1,3-butanediol (BDO) offers a potentially simple and bio-based route to produce 1,3-butadiene (BD). This is an acid-catalyzed dehydration reaction, which is usually carried out over either zeolites or metal oxides. While most of the studies are focused on initial activity, the relationship between nature of the active sites, stability and reaction mechanism remains poorly understood. In this study we show presence of the boron atoms in the zeolite framework along with aluminum enhances stability of the reaction.

title: A mathematical model to predict Weissella viridescens inactivation by ultraviolet radiation
abstract: Lactic Acid Bacteria, including Weissella viridescens, are among the main spoilage microorganisms under modified atmosphere meat products, such as vacuum-packed products. Ultraviolet radiation treatment (UV-C) is a surface food conservation method able to reduce microbial load with minimal quality changes. Thus, the goal of this work was to obtain a mathematical model to predict W. viridescens inactivation under constant and variable UV-C radiation intensities. The Weibull model satisfactorily described the inactivation data.

title: FlaN-a method for calculating morphologies of molecular crystals using a flat nucleus approach
abstract: We present FlaN, a Python program for predicting crystal morphologies from two-dimensional nucleation theory. FlaN constructs polygonal flat nuclei from step-edge energies calculated directly from intermolecular interactions and introduces an edge-density correction factor, K, to account for anisotropic molecular packing. Analysis of over 200 molecular crystal structures shows that inclusion of K reduces sensitivity to user-defined parameters and improves morphology predictions for systems where edge-site densities differ substantially between crystal faces.

title: Development Status, Not Potency: A Data Audit of the Public ADCNet Antibody–Drug Conjugate Evaluation Set
abstract: Background. Deep learning models for antibody–drug conjugate (ADC) activity are evaluated against several distinct prediction tasks: recognizing constructs assembled from familiar components, predicting unfamiliar combinations of known components, and extrapolating to unfamiliar antibodies or payloads — which a single reported accuracy does not separate. A second difficulty arises when the activity label itself combines experimental potency with clinical development status.

title: Beyond the Algorithm: Artificial Intelligence in Drug Discovery from Code to Clinic
abstract: Machine learning (ML) and artificial intelligence (AI) are revolutionizing drug discovery, transforming an inefficient system of trial and error into one based on predictive modeling and data analysis. This comprehensive review on the growing role of computational techniques and tools considers every stage of the traditional drug development pipeline. This paper discusses how novel frameworks, high-throughput data analysis, and molecular dynamics simulations advance the discovery process, from target identification and molecular screening to pharmacokinetic profiling and candidate…

title: Beyond the library ceiling: an accumulation-time rule for electron activated dissociation in data-dependent metabolomics, and the structural information it adds for conjugates, isomers and unknowns in human plasma and urine
abstract: Electron activated dissociation (EAD) reveals what collision-induced dissociation (CID) destroys or ignores: intact conjugates, radical backbone cleavages, and double-bond positions. In untargeted data-dependent acquisition, however, generic settings yield empty spectra, and the few EAD libraries available do not yet cover them. We quantified both limits on a ZenoTOF 8600 with a reversed-phase method in human plasma and urine.

title: In silico assessment of potential protein structural distortion by covalent labeling reagents
abstract: Understanding protein structure is fundamental for studying molecular mechanisms and diseases, as protein structure affects function. Covalent labeling (CL) of proteins is a method to gain structural insights of proteins that may not be amenable to other methods or where the scientific question involved does not require atomic detail. In CL experiments, solvent-accessible residues are chemically modified with specific or nonspecific labels.

title: Synthesizing antikekulene with global antiaromaticity and high stability
abstract: Antiaromaticity is conventionally associated with intrinsic instability, posing a 22 fundamental challenge to the synthesis and isolation of globally antiaromatic hydrocarbons1,2. 23 Most known examples have been realized either in ionic states3,4 or through heteroatom 24 incorporation5-7 to relieve antiaromatic destabilization. Antikekulene (antiK), proposed by 25 Vollhardt in 19868, is an iconic globally antiaromatic hydrocarbon comprising alternating 26 benzene and cyclobutadiene rings whose inner and outer circuits both satisfy the 4n criterion.

title: Sulfonated Poly(phenylene ethynylene) Redirects KLVFFAE Self-Assembly by Suppressing an α-Helix-like Intermediate
abstract: Peptides can assemble along different pathways, and the transient conformations they adopt along the way can influence the structure and properties of the final assemblies. How synthetic polymers alter these intermediate conformations and thereby control peptide assembly remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate how poly(phenylene ethynylene) bearing sulfonate side chains (PPE) changes the assembly pathway of the amyloid-β fragment KLVFFAE (KE).

title: AGA Companion – A Searchable Reaction Database for Automated Glycan Assembly
abstract: Chemical synthesis of oligosaccharides is a critical tool to study the biological functions of glycans. To accelerate glycan synthesis, automated glycan assembly (AGA) was introduced 25 years ago. However, major chemical databases such as SciFinder and Reaxys do not accurately index these automated syntheses, leaving more than two decades of reaction data out of reach for both synthetic chemists and data-driven tools.

title: Spectator Cations Regulate Li+ Solvation in Ionic Liquid Electrolytes
abstract: Organic cations are integral to the ionic network of ionic liquid electrolytes for lithium-ion batteries, yet their participation in lithium-ion solvation offers a design variable beyond salt concentration and anion chemistry. Here, we show that relocating the ether oxygen in the side chain of pyrrolidinium cations changes lithium-anion association and ion transport at a fixed lithium-salt mole fraction. Spectroscopy and theoretical calculations support reduced participation of N-ethoxymethyl-N-methylpyrrolidinium in the coordination network, termed a “spectator cation”.

title: Hives Under Attack- Pesticide Integration and Climate Change Effects on the Physiology and Genetics of Apis mellifera
abstract: Honey bee (Apis mellifera) survival and overall health are threatened by pesticide use and climate change. This review examines the damage these two threats inflict on honey bee population as well as how they interact, creating new, difficult problems to overcome. Pesticides such as imidacloprid and thiamethoxam integrate into bee hives at both the individual and colony level. In the nectar, honey, and wax, pesticides are present in every part of a hive.

title: Water-Accelerated Hydride Transfer in the Oxoammonium-Catalyzed Oxidative Cleavage of Secondary Alkyl Methyl Ethers
abstract: The hydride-transfer oxidation of alkyl ethers by oxoammonium catalysts has hitherto been largely limited to primary substrates because secondary alkyl ethers exhibit intrinsically low reactivity toward hydride transfer. Here, we report that the addition of a small amount of water significantly accelerates the oxoammonium-catalyzed oxidative cleavage of secondary alkyl methyl ethers. The method accommodates both benzylic and unactivated aliphatic ethers, providing carbonyl compounds through selective C–O bond cleavage under mild conditions.

title: Direct Observation of Cooperative Si–H Bond Cleavage by Tris(pentafluorophenyl)borane and Carbonyl Ligands on Tungsten(0) in the Catalytic Hydrosilylation of Imines
abstract: The catalytic hydrosilylation of unsaturated substrates continues to advance through the discovery of unique catalysts that reach hitherto inaccessible reactivity. Here, we report that W(0)-bound CO ligands mediate in cooperation with B(C6F5)3 the heterolytic cleavage of Si–H bonds, which furnishes a siloxycarbyne-like W–CO–Si+ adduct. This is commensurate with the activation of a Si–H bond by a Lewis pair comprising the metal-bound carbonyl oxygen and boron atoms.

title: A Free CAPE-OPEN Electrolyte NRTL Property Package for the CESAR-1 Solvent and a Transferable Equilibrium-Stage Column Methodology Tested on Four Pilot Plants
abstract: A free electrolyte NRTL model of the CESAR-1 solvent (aqueous AMP/piperazine) was implemented in the open-source framework Reaktoro with published parameters and made available as a CAPE-OPEN property package. It reproduces the experimental CO2 solubility in CESAR-1 with an average deviation of 25%, comparable to published models above 60 ◦C and higher at absorber temperatures, and forms the basis of a pilot plant comparison.

title: Resonant doping design for ternary n-type oxides: the case of CdSnO3
abstract: Ilmenite CdSnO3 combines a dispersive, s-type conduction band with a ternary cation framework, which makes it a natural platform to test whether the doping rules established for binary transparent conducting oxides carry over to more complex hosts. Using hybrid density functional theory, we map the intrinsic and extrinsic defect chemistry of CdSnO3 for seven donors (F, Sb, Y, Ta, Nb, W and Mo) across its three sublattices, and combine it with first-principles electron transport.

title: Co-precipitation of Ag2O/Ag over Green Synthesized ZnFe2O4 for Photocatalytic Degradation of Organic Pollutants
abstract: Suppressing the charge carrier recombination in photocatalysis of wastewater based on ZnFe2O4 semiconductor can be achieved through the formation of synergetic effect between the p-n heterojunctions. In this study, Ag/Ag2O was co-precipitated onto green-synthesized ZnFe2O4. Ajuga Integrafolia plant extract was used as a capping and stabilizing agent in the green synthesis of ZnFe2O4. Thermal analysis, phase purity, chemical composition, microstructure, and elemental composition were investigated.

title: Non-Enzymatic Electrochemical Detection of Acephate Using Graphene/Copper Tetraphenylporphyrin Nanocomposite: A Comprehensive Study with Multi-Technique Validation
abstract: The widespread application of organophosphate pesticides in modern agriculture has necessitated the development of rapid, robust, and cost‑effective detection methods for environmental monitoring and food safety assessment. In this study, we report a non‑enzymatic electrochemical sensor based on a reduced graphene oxide–copper tetraphenylporphyrin (RGO–CuTPP) nanocomposite for the detection of acephate, a representative organophosphate insecticide.

title: Multistate Potential Energy Surfaces from an Equivariant Core-Hamiltonian Correction to Semiempirical Configuration Interaction
abstract: Nonadiabatic dynamics needs several coupled potential energy surfaces at once. Fitting each state separately discards the electronic structure that couples them, whereas semiempirical configuration interaction in the style of the orthogonalization-corrected OMx methods obtains all states from one Hamiltonian and thereby keeps the topology of their intersections. We propose to build multistate surfaces by learning inside this Hamiltonian.

title: Organocatalytic hydroboration of allenes promoted by boron-based ionic liquid
abstract: The first protocol for the organocatalytic hydroboration of internal allenes affording Z-alkenylboronates is reported. Efficient and selective addition of HBpin to 1-aryl-3-methylallenes proceeds at room temperature and under solvent-free conditions in the presence of boron-based ionic liquid, 2-butyl-3-ethyl-3-methyl-1,3,2-oxazaborolidinium methanesulfonate, [BEMBox][OMs]. The reaction tolerates various functional groups on the aryl ring and exhibits high regio- and stereoselectivity.

title: Tyrosinase-Like Monooxygenation Activity of Mono- and Dinuclear, Surface-Depositable Cu(I) Pyridinophane Complexes
abstract: Dome-shaped, surface-depositable organometallic complexes are a novel approach for the heterogenization of catalysts. In this context, we synthesized three copper complexes which are supported by different mono- and dinucleating pyridinophane ligands (thiacalixpyridine TCPy, dithiapyridinophane PyPS and thiacalixpyridazine TCPdz). Their monooxygenase activities towards monophenolic substrates were investigated and the influence of cavity size and nuclearity was assessed. While the mononuclear TCPy and PyPS complexes are almost inactive, the dinuclear TCPdz complex exhibits a high reactivity.

title: Mooney Viscosity from Steady-Shear Measurements in a Rubber Process Analyzer
abstract: The Mooney viscosity ML(1+4) is still the most widely used flow parameter of unvulcanized rubbers, although it is a torque and not a viscosity. This work derives the relation between the Mooney torque and the steady-shear viscosity. An analytical solution for the rotor faces and the annular gap, corrected numerically for the corners, gives a conversion factor U(n), which depends only weakly on the flow index n. At a representative shear rate of about 1.2 s −1 , the Mooney viscosity is, therefore, proportional to the viscosity.

title: Flash Communication: PhI(OTf)2 Exists After All.
abstract: We report the observation of the parent PhI(OTf)2. This compound had been incorrectly invoked in many reports, but has never been observed before. Based on work on related systems decomposition pathways for PhI(OTf)2 arising from reaction with TMS-F to generate PhI followed by nucleophilic attack of PhI onto PhI(OTf)2 to generate iodonium cations were identified. This mode of decomposition is mitigated simply by working at lower concentrations, allowing for generation of relatively clean solutions of genuine PhI(OTf)2.

title: Surface Stability of Alloys and Intermetallics during Electrochemical CO Reduction
abstract: Alloy catalysts for electrochemical CO2 and CO reduction are often screened on idealized, bulk-truncated surfaces, yet adsorbates and the applied potential can change which surface is actually stable under reaction conditions. Here, we combine density functional theory with surface thermodynamics to test whether active sites identified from *CO and *H adsorption energies persist in atomically dispersed single-, dual-, and tri-atom alloys, substitutional alloys, and intermetallic compounds.

title: Novel Class of Small Molecules that inhibits Yellow Fever Virus replication
abstract: Yellow fever virus (YFV) is a mosquito-borne virus that causes an acute viral hemorrhagic disease in humans. The high morbidity, recurring large-scale outbreaks, vaccine shortages, and the absence of approved antiviral drugs continue to make YFV a major global health concern. Therefore, the development of safe and effective antiviral agents against YFV remains an urgent priority. In this study, we used a para-menthane monoterpenoid diol and various aldehydes to synthesize a broad series of heterocyclic compounds with hexahydro-2H-chromene and hexahydro-2H-4,6-(epoxymethane)chromene moieties.

title: Structure Responsiveness of fluorinated PEGylated Au Nanoparticles in Physiological Serum.
abstract: Understanding nanoparticle (NP) - protein interactions is critical for controlling colloidal behaviour in biological environments. Here, we study how the introduction of fluorinated moieties into the PEGylated shell of gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) influences interparticle assembly and interactions with protein. Combining microfluidic diffusional sizing (MDS) and small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS), we revealed that exposing fluorinated hydrophobic groups does not compromise the stealth properties of PEG ligands.

title: Antifungals silence a subpopulation of non-albicans Candida
abstract: Antifungal susceptibility tests report how much a drug slows a population, not how that slowdown is distributed among its cells. A culture can lose half its activity because every cell runs at half speed, or because half the cells stop while the rest continue almost unaffected. We distinguished these cases in Candida using a public dataset of 6,227 single-cell Raman spectra from seven strains of C. albicans, C. glabrata andC.krusei,grown inheavy water(D2O) and exposed toamphotericinB,voriconazole, micafungin or flucytosine.

title: Cost-Bounded Evolving Guardrails for Chemistry Protocol Screening via Event-Pair Evidence Retrieval
abstract: Translating a published synthesis paragraph into a machine-actionable protocol is now routine, but judging whether the resulting steps are chemically safe on a given bench is not: frontier models recognise equipment at near-perfect accuracy yet fall to 0.28 accuracy on laboratory safety questions, and whole-text screening of a multi-step paragraph cannot point to which condition–effect pair justifies its verdict.

title: Raman spectra track neoplasia but not malignancy in mouse colon
abstract: Raman spectroscopy is often reported to stage colorectal neoplasia, but validation is usually done at the level of spectra rather than subjects. We reanalysed public spectra from a p53 deletion mouse model (47 mice; 485 spectra of normal mucosa, hyperplasia, adenoma and carcinoma) with leave-one-mouse-out validation, covariate tests and within-scan paired contrasts. Lesions were separated from normal mucosa with a balanced accuracy of 0.79 (95% CI 0.74–0.84). Adenoma and carcinoma were not separated (0.48), although spectrumlevel validation suggested 0.75.

title: ATLAS (Amine-catalyzed Thermal Linkage of Aggregate & Sulfur): Catalytic Valorization of Petroleum Sulfur Copolymer for Scalable, Photothermally Self-Healing Circular Pavements
abstract: Petroleum refining generates massive elemental sulfur surpluses alongside mounting municipal solid waste burdens. Although inverse vulcanization offers a viable synthetic route to convert surplus sulfur into thermoplastic binders, uncatalyzed reactions require elevated temperatures (≥ 159°𝐶), triggering toxic 𝐻 2 𝑆 and 𝑆𝑂 2 off-gassing and severe matrix brittleness. Here, we introduce ATLAS (Amine-catalyzed Thermal Linkage of Aggregate & Sulfur), an eco-efficient paving composite synthesized via low-temperature catalytic inverse vulcanization.

title: Generative molecular dynamics of Li-ion electrolytes conditioned on force-field energy and force
abstract: We generate all-atom molecular dynamics simulation structures of Li-ion battery electrolytes following from molecular centers of mass with a flow-matching model that reads the force field’s energy and its force at its own predicted structure. Molecular dynamics (MD) with a polarizable force field is the reference for electrolyte structure and transport, but each new formulation costs a full simulation. We train a two-stage generative model on around 45,000 NVT simulations of 69 species run with MU-PFF, an in-house polarizable force field.

title: Cooperative OH/CH-based recognition enables lithium chloride binding and extraction
abstract: Lithium chloride is the primary target of ion-pair receptor chemistry aimed at lithium recovery from brines and battery waste. Here, we report the ion-pair receptors for LiCl, built on a resorcinarene scaffold bearing lower-rim CH hydrogen-bond donors, which is crucial for stabilizing the anion in its binding site, combined with OH groups that serve a dual role as anion-binding hydrogen-bond donors as well as Li + coordination sites.

title: Conformation-Dependent Through-Space Interaction: Triplet-State Regulation for Dual Room-Temperature Phosphorescence
abstract: Dual room-temperature phosphorescence (RTP) channels can arise from triplet states of different electronic character within a single molecular emitter, but controlling the contribution of each state remains challenging. Herein, we demonstrate that conformation-dependent intramolecular through-space interactions (TSI) can regulate triplet-state character and enable dual RTP channels from a single molecular emitter. Specifically, two benzo[g]indole (BI) donors are arranged at adjacent positions on a dicyanobenzene acceptor, allowing their intramolecular TSI to vary with molecular conformation.

title: Equation Linking Rydberg Constant, Nuclear Properties, and Periodic Properties of All Atoms
abstract: The problem of the proton charge radius, its correlation with the Rydberg constant, and difficulties in determination of the Rydberg constant using hydrogen atom spectroscopy have been acknowledged. The correlation of proton mass radius with the Rydberg constant is not known. The goal of this study is to derive an all-encompassing equation that unifies the Rydberg constant, the mass radius of the proton, the atomic radii (otherwise called Bohr radii of atoms), and the average ionization energy.

title: What should AI agents know? Explicit knowledge for trustworthy, sustainable materials research
abstract: Artificial intelligence can propose materials, interpret measurements and increasingly coordinate experiments. Yet reliable scientific autonomy requires more than capable models: research systems must preserve what is known, where evidence came from and which actions are justified. We argue that machine-actionable scientific knowledge is essential for trustworthy autonomous research, and that ontologygrounded knowledge graphs are a particularly powerful way of achieving it when scientific meaning must be shared across disciplines, systems and scales.

title: Biomolecular Recognition Programs Fusion and Segregation of Orthogonal DNA Condensates
abstract: Controlling interactions between synthetic compartments is essential for building responsive, reconfigurable molecular systems. Here, we demonstrate that biomolecular recognition programs the fusion of orthogonal DNA-based condensates. To do that, we re-engineered ligand-functionalized DNA nanostars whose orthogonal sticky-end interactions drive phase separation into initially immiscible condensate populations. Addition of a bridging bivalent protein introduces heterotypic connections that promote condensate association, coalescence, and mixing.

title: Phase-Resolved Spectra of Charged Aqueous Solution Interfaces from High-Resolution Broadband Sum Frequency Generation Vibrational Spectroscopy (HR-BB-SFG-VS)
abstract: Phase-resolved sum frequency generation (SFG) spectra provide direct access to the complex nonlinear optical response of interfaces, which can be obtained either through direct phaseresolved measurement or by analyzing intensity spectrum. Recently, we demonstrated that phase-resolved SFG spectra of the neutral air/neat water interface can be obtained from highresolution broadband SFG intensity spectra using multi-peak Lorentzian function fitting (MLFF) with physical constrain with the knowledge of the absolute phase for the ‘free’ O-H peak.

title: Machine Learning-Driven High-Throughput Discovery of Energetic Materials Based on Regioisomeric Pyrazole Scaffolds
abstract: The energy-safety trade-off remains the central challenge in energetic materials design. This study constructs a virtual library of 25,417 derivatives based on two regioisomeric pyrazole scaffolds and trains predictive models using Density Functional Theory (DFT) data from 413 molecules. Unlike conventional approaches, we systematically benchmarked three descriptor families and identified RDKit global physicochemical descriptors as superior to Morgan fingerprints, revealing that global molecular properties govern detonation performance in this regioisomeric system.

title: Clickable zinc fluorescence sensors for live cell imaging
abstract: Zinc fluorescence sensors are widely used to seek a better understanding of the role of so called mobile or labile zinc in the human body. In order to understand biological processes, click-chemistry is often used to immobilize a multitude of different molecules at precise targets. Here, we combine both techniques by incorporating a dibenzoazacyclooctyne (DBCO) residue into two zinc fluorescence sensors of the ZP-family. These new sensors, ZP1(5-Me2en-DBCO) (1) and ZP1(6-Me2en-DBCO) (2), undergo the bioorthogonal, strain-promoted azide-alkyne cycloaddition (SPAAC) with azides.

title: Ligand-Dictated Anisotropic Growth of Cesium Tin Bromide Nanowires at Low Ligand Concentrations
abstract: Cesium tin bromide (CsSnBr 3 ) nanowires (NWs) offer promising optoelectronic properties as alternatives to Pb-based perovskites. However, their synthesis often follows lead-based protocols and overlooks differences in metal–ligand coordination. In this study, we employed the strong coordination between Sn 2+ and an L-type amine ligand to develop a straightforward strategy for obtaining CsSnBr 3 NWs. We reduced the ligand concentration by ~93% compared with their Pb-based counterparts.

title: Crystalline Covalent Organic Frameworks Meet Low Temperature Hybrid Glasses: Synthetic Strategies and Interfacial Interactions
abstract: Hybrid glasses have attracted increasing attention due to their versatility and low melting temperatures, which make them promising matrices for composite formation. Covalent organic frameworks (COFs), in turn, offer high crystallinity, permanent porosity, and tunable chemistry, yet their poor processability limits practical applications. Herein, we combine both to develop COF@Glass composites that overcome this limitation.

title: Parsing the steric and electronic contributions of a second-sphere tryptophan to IsdI-catalyzed heme oxygenation
abstract: Staphylococcus aureus IsdI is a heme oxygenase enzyme that degrades heme to staphylobilin products that are distinct from the biliverdin products of human heme oxygenase. IsdI contains an essential second-sphere tryptophan residue, and the relative steric and electronic contributions of this residue to IsdI-catalyzed heme oxygenation were unclear prior to this work. The W66Y and W66F substitutions similarly decrease the rate of IsdI-catalyzed heme degradation, but the reduction potentials of Tyr and Phe are significantly different.

title: Process Analytical Technology Selection via Predictive Modeling and Human-informed Decision Criteria: Enabling At-line Quality Control in pMDI manufacturing
abstract: Industrial quality assessment often relies on time-consuming offline laboratory methods that delay operational response and limit timely process decisions. At-line process analytical technology (PAT) can reduce this delay by bringing measurements closer to manufacturing operations. Handheld spectroscopy is well suited to this purpose because it enables rapid, non-destructive measurements with minimal sample preparation. Its deployment, however, requires selecting both a device and a measurement protocol.

title: In Vitro Cascade Oxidization of D-Glucose to D-Glucaric Acid by Three Coenzyme-Free Oxidoreductases
abstract: D-Glucaric acid (GA) is one of the top 12 value-added biochemicals with broad applications in the detergent, polymer, pharmaceutical and food industries. The conversion of D-glucose to GA requires full oxidization for both C6 and C1 termini but these highly-selective oxidation of D-glucose remains challenging. Previous in vitro enzymatic pathways have obvious weakness, for example, up to eight enzymes used and the addition of costly coenzyme NAD.

title: Organic Matter by Minimizing Electronic Noise Peaks and Low-abundance Peaks with Few Occurrences
abstract: 21 Peak reproducibility is a major factor that affects the reliability of Fourier transform 22 ion cyclotron resonance mass spectrometry (FT-ICR MS) spectra of dissolved organic 23 matter (DOM), which was addressed by a newly proposed workflow, namely parallel 24 samples representation by similar samples (PSRSS). The performance of the workflow was 25 validated by parallel measurements and experimental replicates.

title: Controlling Guest Selectivity in BINOL-based Pd2L4 Coordination Cages via Endohedral Cavity Functionalization
abstract: BINOL-based chiral Pd2L4 cages were successfully used as supramolecular hosts for the binding of sulfonate guests. Endohedral modification of the cages (OCH2OCH3 vs. OH) enables the modulation of the noncovalent host-guest interactions, which allowed for the chemoselective binding of anthraquinone-disulfonate regioisomers and the stereoselective binding of camphor sulfonate.

title: Highly β-Selective Synthesis of 2-Deoxy N- and C-Glycosides via Photoredox/Cobalt Catalysis: Total Synthesis of Streptcytosine G
abstract: Herein, we report an independently developed photoredox/cobalt-catalyzed radical–polar crossover strategy for the highly β-selective synthesis of 2-deoxy N- and C-glycosides directly from readily available glycals. The synthetic utility of this approach is demonstrated through late-stage glycosylation of bioactive molecules and its application to the total synthesis of streptcytosine G. These findings expand the synthetic applicability of photoredox/cobalt-catalyzed glycosylation to complex carbohydrate substrates and natural product synthesis.

title: MALDI-MS for Fast Analysis of PFOS Partitioning in Bacterial Biomass
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are persistent environmental contaminants whose interactions with biological matrices are increasingly important to characterize. Conventional PFAS analysis in biological matrices using liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) methods typically require extensive sample extraction and cleanup, limiting the throughput of PFAS screening.

title: Synthesis and Electronic Properties of Pentafluorosulfanyldifluoromethyl-Substituted Alkynes
abstract: Pentafluorosulfanyldifluoromethyl-substituted alkynes are synthesized from terminal aryl alkynes and SF5CF2I under 370 nm LED irradiation, providing access to the SF5CF2–C≡C–Ar framework. For phenylacetylene, irradiation at 450 nm favors the vinyl iodide SF5CF2–CH=C(I)–Ph. Comparative calculations reveal connectivity-dependent charge distributions in the alkyne unit. Natural population analysis indicates smaller carbon–carbon charge differences for the CF2-linked architecture than for directly sulfur-substituted analogues, whereas Mulliken analysis gives the opposite trend.

title: Direct observation of valence tautomerism in sublimated molecular sub-monolayers
abstract: This study reports the first observation of a sub-monolayer molecular deposit prepared by sublimation on a conductive substrate of valence tautomerism (VT), an entropy-driven rearrangement of valence electrons between a metal ion and an organic ligand in redox-labile coordination compounds. To this end, a neutral cobalt(II) complex including two iminosemiquinonate redox-active ligands was thermally sublimated under UHV conditions onto highly oriented pyrolytic graphite (HOPG).

title: How Effective is DFTB for Investigating Electrochemical Interfaces? A Study of Metal-Water Systems
abstract: Density-functional tight binding (DFTB) has recently emerged as a computationally efficient alternative to density functional theory (DFT) for modelling metal-water interfaces. However, electrochemical interfaces are inherently grand-canonical, and it remains unclear whether DFTB can reliably capture potential-dependent electronic response beyond equilibrium properties. Here, we systematically benchmark standard self-consistent-charge DFTB for Au(111) and many-body ChIMES-DFTB for Pt(111) against grand-canonical DFT.

title: Site-Dependent Promotion of CO Hydrogenation on Rh(211): Role of Impurity Stability and Step-Edge Charge Distribution
abstract: First-principles calculations were used to investigate direct CO hydrogenation along the step-edge of the Rh(211) surface, modified by substitutional 3d transition metal impurities (X = Ti, V, Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, and Cu) occupying either the step-edge or the terrace lattice site. Impurities at the step-edge site substantially lower the activation barrier relative to pristine Rh(211), with Ti inducing the lowest energy barrier of 0.80 eV, followed by Cr, V, and Mn.

title: Automated Construction of Data-Efficient Machine-Learned Force Fields for Polymers
abstract: General-purpose machine-learned force fields (GP-MLFFs) provide near-first-principles accuracy across broad chemical spaces, but their reliability is limited by training coverage and reference level of quantum mechanics. We present an automated active-learning workflow using the open-source package aims-PAX that builds on GP-MLFF sampling to generate targeted, higher-accuracy reference data for fine-tuning or training models with task-specific architectures.

title: Sunlight-Driven Photo-Reductive Mineralisation
abstract: Perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFASs) are highly persistent molecules whose widespread use and global distribution have created an urgent need to develop effective remediation strategies. Here, we address this research gap by exploiting zinc sulfide (ZnS) for the photo-reductive mineralisation of PFASs under natural sunlight and ambient conditions. We found sulfur vacancies (Vs) within the ZnS lattice, produced during supercritical synthesis, to be responsible for visible-light absorption and enhanced photocatalytic activity.

title: The Same Edit, a Different Outcome: Relational Learning for Cyclic Peptide Permeability
abstract: The same local modification can enhance cyclic-peptide permeability in one chemical background and reduce it in another. Molecular difference learning predicts such changes from structure pairs, yet whole-molecule descriptors can merge stereochemically distinct edits. We test whether the residue relationships changed by an edit supply additional predictive information. Our edit-relational Gaussian process combines parent descriptors and their changes with signed counts of gained and lost residue relationships, preserving stereochemistry and ring, branch and tail connectivity.

title: On-the-fly Neural Network based Kinetic Monte Carlo Simulations of NH3-SCR over Cu-CHA
abstract: Copper exchanged chabazite (Cu-CHA) is the preferred choice for abatement of NOx from lean burn engines. The low-temperature activity depends critically on the presence of paired [Cu(NH3)2]2 + complexes, which are required for O2 adsorption. The pairing of [Cu(NH3)2]2 + complexes has so far been studied by ab initio molecular dynamics or more recently molecular dynamics using machine learning force-fields. An alternative to molecular dynamics is kinetic Monte Carlo (kMC) simulations, which enable simulations over longer time scales.

title: 60-Second NIR Regeneration of H-Phase Nb2O5 from Production Scrap: A Sustainable, Scalable Route to High-Capacity Anode Recovery
abstract: The escalating demand for high-performance lithium-ion batteries has intensified the need for sustainable electrode material recovery strategies that minimise energy consumption and processing time. Here, we report a rapid, energy-efficient nearinfrared (NIR) irradiation approach for the regeneration of niobium pentoxide (Nb2O5) from production scrap comprising a slurry of Nb2O5 active material, polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) binder and carbon black conductive additive.

title: CIPER: Interpretable Permeability Predictions Guide Cyclic Peptide Editing
abstract: Each new analogue in a synthetic cyclic-peptide library requires synthesis and permeability measurement, making the choice of an edit consequential. Molecular difference learning predicts the effect of a modification; we ask whether explicit structural comparisons can also identify the measured analogues supporting its selection or parent retention. CIPER, short for Context-Integrated Potential Edit Regression, learns assay-matched permeability differences through a product of atomic and cyclic-residue kernels. Each prediction is an exact sum of signed training-molecule contributions.

title: Chemoselective Suzuki–Miyaura Cross-Coupling of NHC–Aryl Boranes in the Presence of Boronic Esters: Sequential One-Pot Synthesis of Unsymmetrical Terphenyls from Aryl-Linked Diboron Compounds
abstract: N-Heterocyclic carbene (NHC)–aryl boranes (Ar–BH2–NHC) were found to undergo direct Suzuki–Miyaura cross-coupling (SMC) with aryl bromides under Pd2(dba)3/XPhos catalysis, with no activation step. The reaction tolerated a range of aryl bromides, including one bearing a C–Cl bond that was left untouched. In intermolecular competition with an aryl pinacol boronate (ArBpin), the use of K2CO3 as a base in toluene–H2O delivered the NHC–borane-derived biaryl with 99:1 chemoselectivity.

title: Deciphering Metal-Ion Effects in Engineered Ethylene-Forming Enzymes through Electronic and Electrostatic Reactivity Descriptors
abstract: The selective activation of strong aliphatic C–H bonds remains a fundamental challenge in catalysis due to their high bond dissociation energies and limited chemical differentiation. In biological systems, nonheme FeIV=O intermediates serve as powerful oxidants, enabling challenging C–H transformations such as L-arginine oxidation in ethylene-forming enzymes (EFEs). Here, we investigate how metal substitution modulates the structure, electronic configuration, and reactivity of the EFE active site by replacing iron with manganese and cobalt.

title: The RMSD ceiling: an information limit on geometry-based transition-state metrics
abstract: Machine-learning models for transition-state (TS) geometry prediction are almost universally benchmarked by the root-mean-square deviation (RMSD) of atomic positions, or by the mean absolute error of the interatomic-distance matrix (D-MAE), relative to a reference TS. We show that these Euclidean measures are unreliable proxies for the quantity a practitioner actually needs: whether a predicted geometry optimizes to a genuine TS at a target level of density functional theory. We optimized 520 interpolation-based guesses for 260 reactions from the Transition1x database [Schreiner M., Sci.

title: Phase Resetting of the Pinned Pair of Spirals through Transient Chaotic Dynamics in a Chemical Reaction-Diffusion System
abstract: Excitable chemical reaction-diffusion systems show complex spatiotemporal nonlinear dynamical behaviors. Utilizing the ferroin-catalyzed BZ medium, we characterized the collective dynamics of spiral waves through experimental imaging and numerical simulations with a modified Oregonator model. Here, in this article, we report the emergence of self-regulatory behavior in a Belousov-Zhabotinsky (BZ) medium, where the spirals are pinned to spherical heterogeneity, lose initial phase synchronization on imposition of a perturbation through a mild concentration gradient imposed internally with…

title: nc-CV-MRSF-TDDFT: Spin-complete mixed-reference spin-flip TDDFT with a noncollinear exchange–correlation kernel
abstract: We present nc-CV-MRSF-TDDFT, a spin-complete mixed-reference spin-flip TDDFT with a complete noncollinear exchange–correlation response.
