The theory unifies the two extensions of MRSF-TDDFT, the noncollinear kernel of nc-MRSF and the spin-complete closed–virtual (CV) space of CV-MRSF, in a single response operator. Three parameter-free rules supply every density-functional interaction that the completed CV space requires: the transverse kernel is added wherever exact exchange acts, the Coulomb interaction of a singlet-coupled CV pair is completed with its longitudinal kernel, and the semilocal…

title: On-Demand CO 2 Transport via Magnetically Programmed Orientation of Metal–Organic Framework Crystals in Mixed-Matrix Membranes
abstract: Mixed-matrix membranes (MMMs) offer an energy-efficient alternative to thermally driven industrial separations and a direct route to lower carbon emissions. In metal–organic framework (MOF)-based MMMs, crystallographic orientation can influence molecular transport, yet its contribution is difficult to isolate from other microstructural factors. Here, we exploit the intrinsic magnetic anisotropy of Dy 5 L 6 (OH) 3 (L = 3-amino-4-hydroxybenzoate) crystals to control crystallographic orientation within a 6FDA-DAM matrix without magnetic additives.

title: Dynamic interplay between water and surface carbonates mediates oxygen exchange kinetics in oxide catalysts
abstract: Decorating oxide catalysts with basic oxides decreases surface acidity and lowers the work function, which facilitates electron donation to adsorbed reaction intermediates and thereby enhances oxygen exchange kinetics. However, facilitating electron transfer also renders acid-base-engineered catalysts prone to deactivation by interplay with acidic gas species. The present study investigates the effects of H 2 O and CO 2 on the oxygen exchange kinetics of Ca-decorated SrTi 0.65 Fe 0.35 O 3‑δ .

title: Automated Mapping and Parameterization of Coarse-Grained Force Fields for Dissipative Particle Dynamics
abstract: We present a procedure for the automated mapping and parameterization of coarse-grained (CG) models for dissipative particle dynamics simulations. In our mapping methodology, a given molecule is represented as a graph, and its CG representation consists of a renormalized graph in which groups of vertices (representing heavy atoms) are contracted to single vertices (representing CG particles). Our mapping algorithm identifies functional groups in the molecule and leverages efficient graph-theory-based algorithms to find an optimal mapping for a given mapping scale.

title: Bisnucleophilic Ambident Reactivity of Bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes via Lewis Acid Catalyzed Aldol-Ene Cascade: Diastereoselective Synthesis of Fused Oxabicyclic Scaffolds
abstract: The substantial strain embedded within the compact framework of bicyclo[1.1.0]butanes (BCBs) has established them as versatile 1,3-dipolar synthons for strain-release transformations. However, these advances have exclusively relied on the ambiphilic reactivity of BCBs. In contrast, their ambident reaction modality has remained unexplored, despite its potential to fundamentally expand the reactivity landscape of BCBs and provide access to previously inaccessible chemical space.

title: External Force-free Unpinning and Wave-Break of Pinned Spirals in a Chemical Reaction-Diffusion System
abstract: Excitable media demonstrate patterns; the spiral is one of them. These spiral patterns are also present in the human cardiac system, where they can get pinned in the presence of spatial heterogeneities. Here, we investigate the response of pinned spiral waves in a Belousov-Zhabotinsky (BZ) reaction to an internally generated and temporally evolving chemical heterogeneity, in the form of a gradient produced by Amberlite IR-120 ion-exchange resin beads.

title: A Single Water Molecule Drives a 20-Fold Acceleration in the Gas-Phase Reaction of Iodide with Ozone
abstract: Iodine chemistry has an outsized role in the atmosphere and environment due to its highly reactive nature. Unlike chlorine and bromine, around 80% of atmospheric iodine is emitted directly from the ocean through the reaction of iodide and ozone at the sea surface. Uncertainties remain, however, in the effects of hydration, salinity, temperature, and other factors on this globally significant reaction. Using linear ion-trap mass spectrometry, a single water molecule is shown here to provide a 23 (±6)-fold acceleration to the rate of iodide oxidation.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Generative inverse estimation of 3D atomic coordination from near-edge spectra via equivariant diffusion models
abstract: Extracting 3D atomic coordinates from spectroscopic data is a longstanding inverse problem. We present an equivariant diffusion model that generates the distribution of site-specific 3D structures directly from near-edge spectra (ELNES/XANES). Trained on Si–O crystals, the model achieves radial accuracy comparable to Extended X-ray Absorption Fine Structure (EXAFS) (bond-distance MAE ~ 0.04 Å) but with superior coordination number precision (errors < 2.0% vs. EXAFS ~ 20%). Crucially, it reconstructs full 3D geometries including bond angles, overcoming the limitations of 1D radial distribution analysis. The model shows encouraging, composition-dependent transferability to amorphous systems despite being trained exclusively on crystalline lattices. Application to experimental O K -edge spectra from α -quartz, cristobalite and stishovite demonstrates feasibility for experimental spectra. This generative approach goes beyond conventional template matching, which retrieves structures from predefined references, by enabling the exploration of candidate 3D structures within a learned structural space and providing a step toward automated, quantitative, 3D local-structure inference from spectroscopic data.

title: Multiscale Molecular Simulations in the Age of Exascale Computing.
abstract: The interior of living cells is highly crowded with proteins, nucleic acids, and metabolites-a setting that simultaneously demands large system sizes and long simulation timescales. Exascale computing, now realized on modern supercomputers, offers a qualitatively new opportunity to address this challenge. In this review, we examine how multiscale molecular dynamics simulations-spanning all-atom, coarse-grained, and ultra-coarse-grained representations-are transforming our understanding of macromolecular crowding and liquid-liquid phase separation.

title: Receptor dynamics and kinetic discrimination contribute to selectivity of β1-adrenoceptor antagonists
abstract: Human {beta}1-adrenoceptor (h[beta]1AR)-selective antagonists are widely used to suppress cardiac adrenergic signalling in cardiovascular disease with limited but still clinically relevant inhibition of h[beta]2AR functions in airway and vascular smooth muscle. However, achieving strong subtype selectivity remains challenging because the orthosteric binding sites (OBS) of h[beta]1AR and h[beta]2AR are highly conserved. Here we studied the molecular mechanisms for three highly subtype selective h[beta]1AR antagonists, CGP20712A, NDD713 and NDD825. Three cryo-EM structures were therefore determined for each of the ligands bound to an inactive state of turkey t[beta]1AR in complex with an engineered nanobody fiducial (Nb60.5) to facilitate image processing. There were striking differences in how each antagonist bound to the receptor compared to what was observed in previous antagonist-bound t[beta]1AR and h[beta]2AR structures; these included non-canonical binding of the oxypropan-2-olamine (secondary amine and [beta]-hydroxyl) cores of CGP20712A and NDD825 and the opening of a cleft between transmembrane helices H4 and H5 adjacent to the OBS. Mutagenesis of residues in the extended OBS that differ between h[beta]1AR and h[beta]2AR only partially explained the subtype selectivity. Subsequent kinetic analyses showed that all three ligands associated more rapidly with h[beta]1AR than h[beta]2AR, whereas dissociation effects were ligand dependent. Reciprocal receptor chimeras identified the h[beta]1AR extracellular vestibule as a key factor for fast ligand association. MD simulations further revealed that the cleft opening between H4 and H5 where CGP20712A and NDD825 insert is energetically feasible in h[beta]1AR, but is energetically inaccessible in h[beta]2AR. Together, these results establish that h[beta]1AR selectivity for CGP20712A and NDD825 arises from coordinated effects of OBS recognition, the ligand-entry pathway and receptor dynamics.

title: Lipid-Driven NRF2 Preconditioning Links Estrogen Deprivation to Hepatic Resilience Against Acetaminophen Injury
abstract: Background & Aims: Menopause is associated with a sustained decline in estrogen signaling that profoundly alters hepatic lipid metabolism; however, its impact on the liver response to xenobiotic stress remains poorly understood. Given that acetaminophen (APAP) overdose is a leading cause of drug-induced acute liver failure (DILI) and that sex and age influence susceptibility to hepatotoxicity, we investigated how long-term estrogen deprivation affects the development of APAP-induced liver injury (AP-ILI).

title: Bioinformatics and Machine Learning Internal Validation Reveal the Mechanism by Which β-Ecdysterone Combined with Paeoniflorin Alleviates Oxidative Stress-Induced Damage in Parkinson’s Disease via the Nrf2 Pathway
abstract: Background Oxidative stress induces dopaminergic apoptosis and accelerates Parkinson’s disease (PD). The Nrf2 pathway mediates central antioxidant defense. β-ecdysone (β-Ecd) and paeoniflorin (PF) produce Nrf2-dependent neuroprotection alone, while their combined anti-PD mechanism remains unknown. This study used bioinformatics, machine learning, molecular docking, 100-ns MD simulations and MPTP-PD mice to explore their synergy and Nrf2-mediated neuroprotection. Methods TCMSP screened herbal ingredients. Drug-PD targets and PD DEGs were retrieved from databases and GEO.

title: General Synthesis of Functionalized 1,3-Diamines from Azoarenes and Enoates via Electrochemical Annulation and N–N Bond Cleavage Followed by Chemical Reduction
abstract: Despite the widespread utility of N-substituted 1,3-diamines across numerous fields, their selective synthesis directly from readily available feedstocks remains a long-standing challenge. In this context, we report a room-temperature electrochemical protocol for the synthesis of both symmetrical and unsymmetrical N,N′-disubstituted 1,3-diamines through electrochemical transformation of azoarenes with enoates, followed by convergent reduction of the resulting β-amino amides.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Molecular Mechanophores Based on Stress-Enhanced Exciton Transition between Phosphorescent Probes and Polymer Matrix
abstract: Mechanophores provide an in situ and remote tool for quantifying invisible stress in polymers by photonic signals, offering distinct advantages for stress distribution analysis of large-area surfaces and instrument-free stress observation. However, achieving an ideal mechanophore that integrates with sensitive, reversible, and molecular-level stress sensing is attractive yet challenging.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Adaptive Dynamic Evolution of Substitutional Pt Single Atoms in CeO2 for CO Oxidation
abstract: Platinum-substitutional ceria solid solutions (PtxCe1–xO2) have attracted considerable attention owing to their high stability and activity for low-temperature CO oxidation. However, their catalytic behavior and reactant-induced structural evolution under reaction conditions remain under debate. Here, we investigate the CO-induced structural evolution of substitutional Pt single-atom sites in CeO2(111) and their dynamically catalytic activity for low-temperature CO oxidation by means of density functional theory (DFT) calculations.

title: Editorial: The beginnings of a reset for US science?
abstract: The outcome of the midterms and an influx of federal legislators with science backgrounds offer a chance to start reversing some of the actions of the Trump administration

title: Coupling environmental biosensors to inverter circuits in soil bacteria
abstract: Genetic logic gates, such as inverting NOT functions, are routinely designed and optimised for a narrow set of laboratory-standard chemical inputs. This reliance limits their utility in real-world applications, where engineered chassis must navigate complex, niche-specific signals. Focusing on environmental synthetic biology, we engineered four biosensors responsive to ecologically relevant physical and chemical inputs (iron, oxygen, temperature, and light) and systematically coupled them to three repressor-based NOT logic gates (QacR, SrpR, and LitR) to generate 12 composite sensor-gate circuits. To evaluate cross-host robustness, all constructs were benchmarked in two non-model soil bacteria: Pseudomonas putida KT2440 and Pseudomonas protegens Pf-5. Our findings demonstrate that overall circuit performance is non-additive and cannot be predicted simply by summing individual sensor and gate dynamics. While standalone biosensors reliably detected their cognate inputs, concatenation across regulatory junctions introduced non-linearities, emergent dynamics, and host-dependent effects that caused several pairings to deviate unexpectedly from their predicted behaviour. Furthermore, host context directly governed logic execution: P. protegens Pf-5 exhibited superior overall circuit-processing capacity, whereas specific configurations, such as iron-responsive gates, performed better in P. putida KT2440. All 12 constructs are modularly integrated using the Standard European Vector Architecture (SEVA) format, providing a benchmarked toolkit to program complex information processing in real-world environments.

title: Direct imaging of plasmonic coupling between gold nanoparticles and one-dimensional van der Waals materials
abstract: Hybrids of plasmonic metals and van der Waals (vdW) materials combine electromagnetic field enhancement with the electronic properties of the vdW component, but the studies reported so far concern two-dimensional layers, and the near field at the metal/vdW interface is generally inferred from far-field measurements. Here we report the plasmonic coupling between Au nanoparticles and a one-dimensional (1D) vdW material, NbS3, and measure the near field at the Au-NbS3 contact directly. NbS3 nanowires and nanoribbons were grown by salt-assisted vapor-liquid-solid growth on graphene-covered TEM grids, and atomic-resolution electron microscopy shows atomically sharp Au/NbS3 interfaces. Photon-induced near-field electron microscopy at 1030 nm shows that an Au particle in contact with NbS3 produces a near field of higher intensity and larger extent than an isolated particle of similar size, and that the hot spot at a contact is excited only when the incident polarization is parallel to the particle-NbS3 axis. Finite-difference time-domain simulations reproduce these observations and quantify the dependence of the coupling on the particle-NbS3 gap, the NbS3 thickness, and the dimension ratio of the NbS3 structure. Size-specific Au nanoparticles on NbS3 nanowires enhance the Raman scattering of rhodamine 6G by a factor of 1.8-4.2 relative to Au nanoparticles alone, with a detection limit of 10^-7 M. These results extend plasmonic metal/vdW hybrids to 1D vdW crystals and establish a multimodal approach that correlates the atomic structure of a metal/vdW interface with its nanoscale plasmonic response.

title: Uncertainty Aware AFM-IR Hyperspectral Cube Reconstruction via Convolutional-Attentive Conditional Neural Processes
abstract: Atomic force microscopy-infrared spectroscopy (AFM-IR) maps chemical composition at nanoscale spatial resolution, but the time required to acquire individual spectra limits hyperspectral imaging. Here, we introduce a convolutional-attentive conditional neural process (CACNP), a neural process architecture for reconstructing AFM-IR hyperspectral cubes from sparsely sampled spectra and a small set of structure images, each acquired at a selected wavenumber. The model is trained entirely on synthetic cubes generated from experimental infrared spectra and predicts both spectral intensities and their associated uncertainty. Validation on experimental datasets of poly(methyl methacrylate) and polystyrene particles embedded in epoxy demonstrates accurate reconstruction using only 5% of the available spectra, with competitive performance when compared to other methods. Inference takes less than 0.1 s on 128 X 128 hyperspectral cubes, supporting rapid reconstruction updates, while predictive uncertainty provides a basis for adaptive sampling of localized chemical features. This approach advances autonomous, high-throughput AFM-IR workflows and offers an architecture for accelerating other hyperspectral imaging methods.

title: Self-Supervised Attention-Based Virtual Metrology for CMP MRR Prediction
abstract: Chemical mechanical planarization (CMP) is a critical semiconductor manufacturing process where material removal rate (MRR) is a key metric for process monitoring and advanced process control (APC). Virtual metrology enables MRR estimation from process time series signals, supporting run-to-run(R2R) control and process optimization while reducing reliance on physical metrology. Existing approaches typically rely on simplified linear assumptions or require handcrafted feature engineering. In this paper, we propose Global Regression Pretraining(GREP), a self-supervised, attention-based framework for CMP MRR prediction. GREP learns temporal representations from unlabeled sensor signals through global proxy-target regression, followed by supervised fine-tuning for MRR estimation. The framework is evaluated against a feature-engineered supervised baseline under three conditions: limited labeled data, sensor noise, and temporal process drift. Experiments on the PHM 2016 CMP dataset demonstrate competitive performance under limited labeled-data conditions, with improvements in selected cases and performance largely comparable to the baseline across different labeled-data fractions. Both models exhibit relatively small changes in prediction error with increasing noise, while GREP achieves a 17.0% RMSE reduction in the final temporal interval.

title: Humidity-modulated Ostwald Step Rule in $\rm FAPbI_3$ Martensitic Transitions
abstract: Experimental observations reveal a dual role of moisture in $\rm FAPbI_3$ phase transitions. During fabrication at high temperatures, humidity improves the quality of the perovskite ($α$ phase) films, whereas at low service temperatures, humidity accelerates degradation of the photoactive $α$ phase into the photo-inactive hexagonal $δ$ phase. Despite extensive experimental evidence, the microscopic mechanisms by which moisture modulates phase stability and transition pathways remain unknown. Here, using large-scale atomistic simulations powered by an ab initio machine-learned potential, we reproduce the experimentally observed increase in the $δ$-to-$α$ transition temperature under increased humidity. Our simulations reveal a layered metastable intermediate along the Burgers transition pathway that exhibits a strong affinity for water. The competing water uptake of this intermediate and the $δ$ phase governs the humidity dependence of transition kinetics. These findings elucidate the dual role of moisture in perovskite phase transitions and demonstrate how environmental species can stabilize metastable intermediates and reshape transition pathways, providing an environment-dependent perspective on Ostwald's step rule.

title: Interpretable Machine Learning Accelerates Rational Design of Dual-Site Catalysts for Synergistic Catalytic Aerobic Oxidative Synthesis of Benzimidazole
abstract: The aerobic oxidative synthesis of benzimidazole requires heterogeneous catalysts that combine high activity with practical stability. Because conventional catalyst optimization depends heavily on laborious experimental screening, we established an interpretable machine learning (ML) workflow to accelerate catalyst selection and identify the variables governing performance.

title: Can lithium mining take off in Europe?
abstract: Europe wants to source its own lithium by 2030, but domestic mining projects face an uphill battle

title: Studying temperature-induced decrease of spontaneous polarization in PbTiO$_3$ from vibrational amplitude
abstract: PbTiO$_3$ is a typical ferroelectric polarization induced negative thermal expansion (NTE) material at a wide range of temperature. The elegant TiO$_6$ octahedron is used to study the polarization and NTE, whereas lacking its quantitative characterization. In this work, we propose a concise projection of vibrational amplitude to describe anisotropic distortion of atoms with temperature based on $ab$ $initio$ molecular dynamics simulations. We find that the huge negative mode Grüneisen coefficient is mainly from the different vibrational modes of the TiO$_6$ octahedral rotation at two boundary symmetry points in tetragonal phase along $c$ direction. The potential energy surface as a function of amplitude suggests the $c$-axis compression facilitates the TiO$_6$ octahedral rotation. We show that the vibrational mode of TiO$_6$ octahedral rotation around negative-expansion axis can promote spontaneous polarization reduction with increasing temperature, making transformation of PbTiO$_3$ from tetragonal to cubic phase occur, via the projected amplitude, potential energy surface, and forces of individual atoms.

title: Stable ring-polymer molecular dynamics without Fourier transforms: a linear-scaling bead-space Cayley propagator
abstract: Ring-polymer molecular dynamics (RPMD) builds zero-point energy and tunnelling into classical trajectories and is widely used for bimolecular rate coefficients. At low temperature it requires many beads, and the stiff ring-polymer springs then limit the integrator. The Cayley modification of the free ring-polymer step removes this limit, but it has so far been formulated mode by mode, which requires Fourier transforms of every degree of freedom at every step. Here we show that, in bead coordinates, the Cayley step reduces to one cyclic tridiagonal solve for the midpoint of the step, with a matrix that depends only on the number of beads $P$, the temperature and the time step, and not on the atomic masses. The bead-space step is exactly the normal-mode Cayley map: it conserves the free ring-polymer energy, preserves the free ring-polymer Boltzmann distribution, and is stable for any $P$ whenever $ΩΔt<2$ for the highest physical frequency $Ω$. A Thomas recursion with a rank-two Woodbury correction solves it in about $18P$ operations per degree of freedom without pivoting, with a condition number bounded by $1+(ω_PΔt)^2$, and the inverse matrix decays geometrically with bead separation, so the step is local in bead index. Implemented in the open-source PyRPMD package, the propagator reproduces normal-mode Cayley to $1.5\times10^{-15}$ for up to 2048 beads and its cost grows linearly with $P$. For direct RPMD (dRPMD), which has so far integrated the springs explicitly, these properties raise the stability limit on the time step 23--29-fold in published low-temperature settings; at \SI{20}{K} with 3072 beads, the Cayley step conserves the ring-polymer energy as well as velocity Verlet does with a time step about ten times larger, while leaving the low-lying internal modes that govern spurious resonances essentially unchanged.

title: Dynamic Tunneling a Prior Phenomenon to Intermediate Resistive States in Defect Engineered Mn-SrTiO3 RRAM Devices
abstract: Resistive random-access memory devices work under the principle of resistive switching from high resistive state to low resistive state under applied electric field. In this work, 2%Mn doped SrTiO3, devices were fabricated using PLD in which, the defects are engineered such that the conducting filament formation is expected to have two oppositely charged defects: a) presence of Mn3+ dopants, giving rise to a negatively charged Mn and Ti and b) single and double positive oxygen vacancies. This process of two filaments emanating from both the electrodes has shown enhancement in the resistive switching characteristics aiding in forming-free switching that exhibits over 102 as ON/OFF ratio with a memory retention beyond 103 seconds at a low read voltage of 0.1V. All devices demonstrated a stable bipolar resistive switching dominated by conduction filament formation resulting from a synergic effect of oxygen vacancies and the varying oxidation states of Mn based negative defects that propagates toward each other under bias. The formation of defect-based filaments around the bias electrode was evidently observed using XPS of the devices before and after switching. A dynamic tunnelling process is observed as an intermediate process before the conduction filament forms in the SET region and following the snapping in the RESET region. Conduction filaments being heavily doped localizes conduction pathways with a small finite tunnelling barrier gap that are instantaneously formed and ruptures during switching cycles. The dynamic tunnelling behavior gives rise to a tiny spike in current and is observed at the intermediate resistive states which are potential for multi-state usage of these devices. Overall, Mn-STO devices of varying thicknesses show promising retention features and defect engineering offers control over single and/or multi-states memory.

title: Induced Structural Disorder Enables High Ionic Conductivity and Capacity in Li2Fe1− x Mn x Cl4 Cathodes
abstract: The development of high-energy-density solid-state batteries is aided by the discovery of ionically conductive cathode active materials which can enable the production of cathode composites with high active material loadings. Here, we show that the ionic conductivity of Li2FeCl4 can be more than doubled by increasing the structural disorder via a facile mechanochemical and low-temperature annealing procedure. We find that the metastable Fd3̅m Li2FeCl4 phase produced by mechanochemical synthesis undergoes a room temperature structural re-ordering on the scale of months, which lowers the ionic conductivity and raises concerns for the shelf-life of metastable materials. We demonstrate that the structural disorder can be “locked-in” by introducing Mn2+ into the system without significantly impacting the ionic conductivity. We further elucidate the origin of the phase transitions and the role of enthalpic stabilization on ionic conductivity through density functional theory and machine-learning force field molecular dynamics calculations. These reveal a 3-dimensional Li+ conduction pathway in the disordered structure, which is not present when the material is ordered. By engineering high-conductivity disordered, Fd3̅m, phases of Li2FeCl4 and Li2Fe0.75Mn0.25Cl4, solid-state batteries containing zero catholyte are demonstrated with high voltage plateaus of 3.7 V and capacities of 115 mAh/gCAM and 90 mAh/gCAM, respectively. Considering the high cathode loadings, we demonstrate that the materials Li2FeCl4 and Li2Fe0.75Mn0.25Cl4 can be used to produce solid-state battery cathodes with higher energy densities than that of LiFePO4, with similar cost effectiveness.

title: ORCHID-SAGE: Fully Reproducible CALPHAD Assessment from Evidence to Phase Diagram
abstract: Knowledge of phase stability is the first requirement for materials design, and predicting the conditions under which new materials can be synthesized has become a key capability of self-driving laboratories (SDLs). For inorganic materials, notably alloys, these predictions come from thermodynamic databases built with the CALPHAD method. Building a database, however, requires expert judgment at many steps, and because these decisions are rarely recorded, others can use a database but cannot regenerate or update it. Machines can already collect the data, build a first model with machine-learned interatomic potentials and refine it against experiments. The assessment itself, the sequence of judgments that turns these parts into a reliable database, is still carried out by human experts. We argue that it can be automated reproducibly only if the expert knowledge behind an assessment is encoded in formal protocols, so that an assessment delivers a record of its construction and not only its parameters. We introduce ORCHID-SAGE, a standard that organizes this record into reproducible and automatable protocols. In this first attempt, applied to Cr-Ni, the database was regenerated from its record by a script on a second machine, by an AI agent working only through the Model Context Protocol (MCP) and by a refit from public sources only, with the same predictions. Recorded in this way, a database need no longer be fixed at publication but can be updated by AI agents as SDLs and other sources provide new evidence, while the judgment remains with people and on the record.

title: HARMONY: an efficient and accurate deep learning framework for prediction of experimental vibrational spectra
abstract: Predicting experimental vibrational spectra requires both efficient molecular calculations and a reliable mapping from theoretical vibrations to measured signals. Here we introduce \textbf{HARMONY}, a two-stage deep-learning framework that bridges this gap using harmonic spectra as physical anchors. Equivariant neural networks directly predict atomic forces and spectroscopic tensors for rapid harmonic-spectrum construction, while HarmoNet combines these spectra with molecular topology and measurement metadata to predict experimental infrared and Raman spectra. HARMONY achieves mean cosine similarities of 0.912 for infrared and 0.907 for Raman spectra, with a mean inference time of 2.12~s per molecule, approximately 600-fold faster than the evaluated DFT workflow. Beyond forward prediction, HARMONY improves inverse molecular inference through pseudo-experimental pretraining and spectral verification of candidate structures. Integrating HARMONY and Vib2Mol as scientific tools within a general-purpose agent enables adaptive candidate generation and verification. With molecular formulas provided, the resulting Vib2Mol--HARMONY Agent achieves Top-1 recall of 70.53\% on NIST using infrared spectra and 83.33\% on SDBS using combined infrared and Raman spectra. Fine-tuning with 19 amino-acid controls and eight peptides further increases mean Raman cosine similarity from 0.669 to 0.896 on 15 held-out peptides. HARMONY establishes harmonic anchoring as a practical connection between molecular physics, experimental spectroscopy and adaptive molecular structure elucidation.

title: MutAtlas: A PDB-Wide Energy-Guided Atlas of Protein Mutation Effects
abstract: Protein mutation effect prediction is fundamental to protein engineering and disease variant interpretation, yet experimentally measured mutation data remain accurate but extremely sparse. To provide scalable supplementary mutation signals, we construct a PDB-wide mutation augmentation dataset that exhaustively enumerates single-site substitutions on experimentally resolved protein structures and aligns mutation signals from physics-based energy models, protein language models, and inverse folding models. Large-scale analysis under a unified mutation preference representation reveals substantial differences in the consistency, concentration, and substitution patterns of mutation distributions across models, indicating that disagreement is pervasive and reflects conflicting inductive biases rather than random noise. Motivated by these observations, we propose an unsupervised multi-source mutation preference distillation framework that learns from relative mutation preferences while explicitly modeling cross-source disagreement. Without using any experimental mutation labels during training, our approach achieves the best overall performance among the evaluated zero-shot baselines and naive multi-source fusion strategies on ProteinGym. We release the dataset and evaluation pipeline to support reproducible studies of protein mutation effects.

title: Sign changing pairing in single layer FeSe/SrTiO3 revealed by nonmagnetic impurity bound states
abstract: The discovery of high-temperature superconductivity in single layer FeSe epitaxially grown on SrTiO3(001) substrates has instigated extensive debate over whether its pairing symmetry is conventional sign-preserving s-wave or unconventional sign-changing. Here we probe the pairing state for single layer FeSe/SrTiO3 grown by molecular beam epitaxy using scanning tunneling microscopy/spectroscopy. We observe robust in-gap bound states induced by non-magnetic Fe-vacancy defects within the Fe-plane, which exhibit strong spatial electron-hole asymmetry with two-fold symmetry in hole states and four-fold in electron states. The bound states exhibit no energy shift or splitting under an applied magnetic field, consistent with a sign-changing order parameter.

title: Proteome-wide reanalysis identifies coverage and error-rate limits on acquired lysines in cancer
abstract: Missense mutation in cancer creates acquired lysines, residues present in tumor cells and absent from normal cells in the same patient. The class holds 295,411 sites across 20,365 genes and falls on driver hotspots more often than other substitutions (odds ratio 1.68). Yet re-searching 42 proteomic experiments with a mutation-aware database recovers the mutant peptide in 0.63% of 8,470 site-in-cell-line observations, because a new lysine is a new cleavage site and the peptide it creates runs 6 residues against 13 for the wild type. Reported error rates do not hold either. Burden-matched entrapment puts the realized false-discovery proportion at 4.70% before score filtering, against 1% reported. Measured by competitive activity-based protein profiling across four cell lines, ligandability reproduces at the site level, no compound descriptor tested predicts it, and structure predicts it poorly at AUC 0.617. Acquired lysines are structurally ordinary, so the barrier is detection rather than chemistry.

title: Electrode-Side Catalytic Regulation Directs Electrolyte Decomposition for Stable Silicon Anodes.
abstract: The electrochemical stability of silicon anodes is critically influenced by the initial decomposition pathways of fluorine-containing electrolyte species, which dictate the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) composition and stability. However, existing strategies primarily rely on electrolyte fluorination or artificial interphases to indirectly regulate SEI chemistry, whereas precise electrode-side regulation of fluorine-containing electrolyte decomposition remains challenging.

title: Spontaneous Neuronal Activity in Autism Spectrum Disorder: Insights from Human and Animal Studies
abstract: Developmental spontaneous neuronal activity (SNA) plays an instrumental role in the generation of precise brain circuits. Spontaneous activity patterns guide neuronal differentiation, synaptic refinement, and circuit formation; consequently, perturbations in these activity patterns can profoundly influence brain network organization. Growing evidence suggests that mutations in autism-associated genes lead to alterations of the SNA pattern during early brain development, thereby giving rise to the behavioral features of autism spectrum disorder (ASD).
venue: The Neuroscientist : a review journal bringing neurobiology, neurology and psychiatry

title: Anti -Dihydroxylation-Enabled Dual-Resolution Profiling and Imaging of Fatty Acid C═C Bond Isomers
abstract: Lipids are essential for membrane structure, signaling, and stress adaptation. Their diverse biological roles are largely dictated by the presence of C═C bonds in unsaturated fatty acids (FAs), which vary in both position and geometry. However, unambiguous characterization and in situ mapping of these two structural features have remained longstanding analytical challenges. Here, we present a stereochemistry-preserved chemical derivatization strategy coupled with trapped ion mobility spectrometry-tandem MS (TIMS-MS/MS), enabling complete resolution of both FA C═C bond position and geometry within a single workflow. This approach facilitates rapid and quantitative profiling of dynamic cis–trans isomerization in bacteria under diverse stress conditions and, notably, reveals a previously unrecognized dose-dependent antibiotic adaptation mechanism in Pseudomonas aeruginosa, a multidrug-resistant pathogen. To translate this strategy to spatially resolved analyses, we developed an in situ derivatization workflow for mass spectrometry imaging, which uncovers the spatial heterogeneity of FA isomers in proximally cocultured, clinically relevant polymicrobial pathogens. These findings highlight colony-specific spatial dynamics of cis and trans lipid isomers and suggest lipid-mediated metabolic interactions between co-occurring microbial species. Together, this integrated platform enables both quantitative and spatial interrogation of lipid isomerization, providing new opportunities to systematically investigate its roles in microbial physiology, pathogenesis, and beyond.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Control of Charge Carrier Dynamics and Bandgap Renormalization in CdS Quantum Dot Hybrids by Interface Polarity
abstract: Charge carrier dynamics in wurtzite CdS quantum dots (QDs) form the basis for applications in optoelectronics and photocatalysis. We demonstrate that the quantum dynamics, energy gaps, and energy level alignments at CdS QD interfaces can be controlled by the polarity of the CdS QD surface. By performing nonadiabatic molecular dynamics simulations within a density-functional tight-binding framework, we demonstrate a strong dependence of photoinitiated processes in CdS QDs/graphene nanoribbon (GNR) hybrids on interface polarity.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: How Should Planning Agents ReSHAPE Their Search Space?
abstract: Planning agents and benchmarks treat a user's initial specification as fixed. Yet the requests users write exclude plans they would gladly take, since they rarely discover the possible trade-offs they would accept until seeing the options. Agents already revise requests through interaction, but whether this helps planning is unknown. We formalize this step as the ReSHAPE task, which judges a revision by whether its search space matches the acceptable plans and a planner finds one there. Using ReSHAPE Planter, which builds instances from planning benchmarks with a human-validated simulated user, we analyze 5,800 agent-revised specifications in travel and shopping. We find that reshaping matters: one correct trade-off makes the same planner reach an acceptable plan up to 4.6x as often, and search space quality predicts what the planner finds. Current agents, however, admit at most 32% of the acceptable plans, where that trade-off alone admits over 52%, because they ask about preferences instead of showing plans; in travel, showing plans raises F1 by 9.7 points over asking, with two model families. Planning agents should thus treat a request as a hypothesis to test against the user's reactions to concrete plans to recognize user trade-offs.

title: Why "quantum spin liquids'' are quantum singlet liquids
abstract: The last couple of decades have seen enormous theoretical and experimental research efforts aimed at finding quantum spin liquids (QSLs) in geometrically frustrated (GF) magnetic materials. Experimental demonstrations of QSLs are challenging due to the indirect character of possible QSL signatures and the presence of impurities in materials, which may destroy or obscure a QSL. At the same time, theoretical literature often lacks consensus about the ground states of quantum spins on even the simplest GF magnetic lattices. We summarize experimental evidence that in the impurity-free limit, available GF magnetic materials that do not develop magnetic order at low temperatures would form {\it a quantum singlet liquid}, i.e. a disordered state of non-magnetic excitations. We further confirm the existence of such a singlet liquid and its gapless character with theoretical arguments. Such a liquid manifests itself in the thermodynamics of GF magnets while having no magnetic features at low temperatures.

title: Compensated Grid-Based Hybrid Exchange - A Simple, Accurate, Efficient, and Differentiable Recipe for Large-Scale Molecular Systems
abstract: A compensated grid-based approach is developed for hybrid exchange in large-scale molecular systems. The method uses a symmetrically overlap-fitted grid-based exchange approach, with fitting performed in the orthonormalized atomic orbital basis. This fitting is augmented with a superposition-of-atomic-densities difference-density (dSCF) partitioning of the exchange energy, yielding the finished compensated grid-based exchange approach. The complete method is found to have orders of magnitude reduction of absolute and relative error properties versus raw grid-based exchange, and remains analytically differentiable. The method is easy to implement and provides efficiency gains over GPU integral-direct techniques for high quality and/or augmented basis sets. Library functions to help users implement the method in their own quantum chemistry codes are provided in the recently-shipped cuEST v0.3 library.

title: Multi-reference variational states resolve stripe selection and local $d$-wave pairing in the Hubbard model
abstract: Whether stripes compete with $d$-wave superconductivity or promote pairing through fluctuations remains unsettled in the two-dimensional Hubbard model. Using multi-reference neural variational auxiliary-field quantum Monte Carlo (MR-nVAFQMC) at $U/t=8$, we superpose unpaired Slater determinants across stripe periods and domain-wall positions, reaching variational energies competitive with leading benchmarks on periodic lattices up to $32\times32$ sites. For cuprate next-nearest-neighbor hopping ($t'/t=-0.2$), diagonal hopping preserves electron-doped antiferromagnetism while kinetically frustrating hole motion into Yamada stripes with a dome of short-range connected $d$-wave pairing. At $1/8$ hole doping, hole delocalization across antiphase spin boundaries outweighs on-site repulsion, splitting the filled stripes of the pure model into half-filled walls with strong local pairing. Coherently delocalizing shifted walls strongly suppresses static charge modulation yet leaves short-range pairing unchanged, showing that local pairing is intrinsic to half-filled walls rather than driven by stripe fluctuations. Across intervening antiferromagnetic domains, however, pairing correlations become unresolved at one stripe period and beyond. Both parameter transfer to larger lattices without reoptimization and deep benchmark checkpoints retain stripe spin order without resolving long-range pairing, within uncertainties allowing weak superconductivity. Half-filled antiphase walls thus generate local $d$-wave pairs, whereas suppressing static stripe order alone yields no resolved coherence across stripes in the states studied.

title: Structure of human hephaestin reveals a homodimer anchored to the cell membrane
abstract: Hephaestin (Heph) is a membrane-bound ferroxidase that oxidizes ferrous ion (Fe2+) exported by ferroportin (Fpn) to ferric ion (Fe3+), enabling iron loading onto transferrin for systemic delivery. Loss-of-function mutations in Heph cause iron accumulation in intestinal enterocytes and systemic iron deficiency in animal models, underscoring its role in iron export. Heph has a large extracellular domain anchored to the cell membrane by a single transmembrane helix. However, full-length Heph has not previously been purified, and our understanding of its structure and function remains incomplete.

title: S-adenosylmethionine supply controls DNA methylation turnover in synovial sarcoma
abstract: Background: Methionine is the nutrient source of the metabolite S-adenosylmethionine (SAM) used to methylate chromatin for regulation of gene expression. Disruptions to this metabolic supply, including nutritional deficiency of certain B vitamins, alter chromatin methylation and have been implicated in tumor growth. Objective: To define how cellular SAM supply controls DNA methylation dynamics and the disruption of oncogenic gene expression in synovial sarcoma. Methods: Cell line models of synovial sarcoma were treated with the DNA methyltransferase inhibitor azacitidine or the small-molecule MAT2A inhibitor AG-270, which blocks SAM synthesis from methionine. Intracellular SAM concentrations were quantified by liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry. Global DNA methylation rates were measured by stable isotope tracing with [2H3-methyl]-methionine. Genomic sites of altered DNA methylation were identified by EM-seq and the associated transcriptional changes measured by RNA-seq. Results: Inhibition of SAM synthesis reduced intracellular SAM concentration from 94 uM to 5.6 uM (p value < 0.0001) at 24 hours. This was associated with a 19% decrease (p value < 0.0001) in the global 5-methyldeoxycytosine turnover rate, while total DNA methylation levels were maintained. In contrast to the global DNA hypomethylation induced by azacitidine, SAM depletion resulted in a redistribution of DNA methylation with loss at 252 and gain at 206 genomic sites, and the transcriptional response to SAM depletion was not associated with changes in promoter methylation at the altered genes. Both azacitidine and SAM depletion activated mesenchymal genes, while suppressing cell cycle progression. Conclusions: Metabolic supply of SAM is a major regulator of DNA methylation turnover providing a mechanism by which nutritional or genetic disruptions to SAM metabolism can alter chromatin methylation and gene expression.

title: SUMOylation Regulates IRF2BP2 Nuclear Localization and Stability
abstract: Interferon Regulatory Factor-2 Binding Protein 2 (IRF2BP2) is a transcriptional cofactor implicated in diverse biological processes. Although it functions primarily as a repressor, it can also activate gene expression. However, the mechanisms governing IRF2BP2 regulation remain poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that IRF2BP2 interacts with UBE2I, the SUMO E2 ligase, and undergoes multi-SUMOylation, which enhances its nuclear localization. We further show that IRF2BP2 nuclear import is importin-{beta}-dependent and requires the functional nuclear localization signal (NLS). IRF2BP2 preferentially accumulates in transcriptionally active euchromatin in both resting and S-phase cells, consistent with its role in transcriptional control. We further reveal that SUMOylation contributes to IRF2BP2 stability. Moreover, IRF2BP2 is also ubiquitinated, predominantly through K6-linked ubiquitin chains, a non-proteolytic modification that aligns with our observation that IRF2BP2 is not degraded by the proteasome. Together, these findings identify SUMOylation and non-proteolytic ubiquitination as key mechanisms regulating IRF2BP2, highlighting a novel SUMO1-NLS-importin-{beta}-dependent pathway that governs its localization.

title: An anaerobic cell-free protein synthesis formulation for the in vitro study of oxygen sensitive proteins
abstract: Anaerobic microbes harbor unique enzymes and metabolic pathways with potential biotechnological applications, yet these microbes remain difficult to study and engineer. Research is limited by the labor-intensive workflows required to maintain anoxic environments and the lack of genetic tools available for non-model anaerobes. Here, we present an anaerobic cell-free protein synthesis (CFPS) platform for the in vitro study of oxygen-sensitive enzymes. This study establishes two methods for conducting anaerobic CFPS, achieving an anoxic environment by (1) sparging with inert gas or (2) lyophilizing to remove oxygenated water. We show the functionality of our anaerobic CFPS formulation by producing oxygen-independent fluorescent protein reporters and a [4Fe-4S] cluster pyruvate:ferredoxin oxidoreductase (PFOR) with a specific activity of 5.2 {+/-} 0.3 x 10-4 U/{micro}L cell-free extract. This highly modular platform will allow study of diverse oxygen-sensitive proteins and requires only minor modifications to commonly used CFPS workflows.

title: The diamond paradox: Scientists describe the path to the most stable structure
abstract: Researchers from Skoltech (part of the VEB.RF Group) and MISIS University have figured out why graphite turns into an unexpected form of diamond under high pressure. Instead of the familiar cubic diamond, the first structure to form is metastable lonsdaleite—a hexagonal form of diamond in which carbon atoms are arranged in layers differently than in ordinary diamond.

title: Controlled Growth and Disorder Mitigation of GaAs1-xSbx/InAs Core-Shell Quantum Wires
abstract: We report the growth and transport properties of GaAs1-xSbx/InAs core-shell nanowires. Compared with the well-studied GaAs-InAs system, incorporating Sb substantially reduces the lattice mismatch between the core and shell. Accordingly, both the nanowire crystal quality and device performance improved significantly. Increasing x from 0.15 to 0.35, the density of crystalline defects, such as stacking faults in the InAs shell, decreases by half. Moreover, the field-effect mobility increases from 3850 cm2/Vs to 4800 cm2/Vs, consistent with the reduction of the lattice mismatch. The incorporation of Sb makes the nanowire easier to pinch off via the gate voltage, enhancing the electric field tunability over the nanowire. Magneto-conductance measurements reveal Aharonov-Bohm-like oscillations, suggesting a phase-coherent tubular InAs shell. Our results identify lattice mismatch as a critical disorder source in core-shell nanowires and provide a practical route toward low-disorder core-shell quantum devices.

title: Optically-detected room-temperature spin-coherence from the GaV$^-$ in diamond
abstract: Solid-state quantum defects (point crystal imperfections with optically addressable spins) are among the most promising platforms for quantum information science due to their long-lived electron and nuclear spin lifetimes. The negatively-charged nitrogen-vacancy (NV$^-$) and negatively-charged group IV vacancies (G4V's) in diamond are some the most promising quantum defects but, the NV$^-$ is highly susceptible to charge noise and has low emission from its zero-phonon line while the G4V's require low operating temperatures. Here we report the physical properties of the newly discovered negatively-charged gallium-vacancy in diamond, GaV$^-$. We find that the GaV$^-$, created through FIB implantation and high-pressure high-temperature annealing, exhibits a combination of the best properties of both the NV$^-$ and G4V's: optically-detectable spin coherence at room temperature ($T_2(293K) = 1.06 μ$s), a large Debye-Waller factor $\sim$0.4, a short radiative lifetime ($\sim$3.83 ns), strong temperature dependence of the zero-field splitting (16x that of the NV$^-$), and charge-noise-protected D$_{3d}$ symmetry. These features (along with improved performance at low temperature) position the newly discovered GaV$^-$ as a key resource for quantum sensing, networking, and computation.

title: Self-organized criticality in a mammalian RNA-interference circuit
abstract: Living systems have been argued to operate near critical points, but their relevance at the cellular level is poorly understood. Critical states allow for a high sensitivity to external inputs and maximal information transfer and display fluctuations at all scales. Critical points are very special, and require the fine tuning of a control parameter, which is hard to reconcile with the robustness of living cells. Self-organized criticality (SOC) proposes that feedback, rather than tuning, brings a system to its critical point.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Otoscopy for Tympanic Membrane Pathologies: A State-of-the-Art Scoping Review
abstract: This paper aimed to conduct a systematic search within a scoping review framework and provide a critical narrative appraisal of the current literature on artificial intelligence (AI) applications for tympanic membrane (TM) image analysis in the diagnosis of ear infections, with a focus on methodological rigor, dataset characteristics, and clinical applicability. A comprehensive search was performed across various online databases (Scopus, PubMed, Google Scholar, Embase, IEEE Xplore, and SPIE Digital Library) to identify studies published up to June 30, 2024. Studies employing AI for the analysis or classification of TM images in ear disease diagnostics were included. Inclusion and exclusion criteria were predefined. Data extraction covered dataset properties, imaging modalities, AI models, validation strategies, and performance metrics. The level of evidence, potential sources of bias, and methodological rigor were assessed qualitatively. Eighty-three studies met inclusion criteria, encompassing 90 experimental results. Considerable heterogeneity was observed regarding dataset size, image quality, device types, labeling protocols, and AI models. Most studies relied on small, private datasets, limiting model generalizability. While deep learning methods-especially convolutional neural networks-achieved high classification accuracies, methodological limitations included inconsistent data augmentation, imbalanced datasets, and lack of external validation. Few studies employed multidisciplinary teams or standardized protocols. Despite notable advances in AI-driven TM image analysis, direct comparison of studies remains challenging due to substantial heterogeneity and methodological shortcomings. A meta-analysis or systematic review was not performed, as quantitative synthesis would be misleading due to substantial data and labeling heterogeneity, wide methodological diversity, and a widespread lack of external validation across the included studies. Future research should prioritize larger, diverse, and well-annotated datasets, adoption of standardized protocols, and interdisciplinary collaboration to improve the clinical translation and reliability of AI-based diagnostic tools for ear infection management.
venue: The journal of international advanced otology

title: Associative Learning and Memory Erasure in a Synthetic Multicellular System
abstract: Learning is a basic form of adaptation that organisms display from neural systems to single cells. In associative learning, the pairing of two stimuli lets one of them evoke the response to the other. Engineering this behavior in a living cell is difficult, because coincidence detection, memory, and conditional readout must be wired into a single regulatory network. Here we build a consortium of five E. coli strains that distributes the operations of associative learning and communicates through one diffusible quorum-sensing signal. The same signal acts as the memory trace.

title: Bulk CMSX-4 Single-Crystal Builds via Laser-Directed Energy Deposition: Epitaxial Stability and Microstructure Evolution
abstract: Single-crystal processing of Ni-based superalloys using laser-directed energy deposition (L-DED) is extremely challenging, given the interplay of a number of processing parameters. In this work, we develop strategies to maintain single-crystal growth in long cylindrical rod geometries by combining dynamic adjustment of laser power, informed by in-situ infrared thermal feedback, with a simulation-guided external cooling system. This combined approach ensures optimal heat extraction during additive manufacturing, maintaining near-steady-state conditions at the solidification interface and extending continuous epitaxial growth to nearly twice the build height achievable through process control alone. The developed strategy results in continuous single-crystal growth, as validated by electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD). The steady-state nature of solidification is revealed through the near-constant primary dendritic arm spacing. Further, the heat-treatment is optimized by reducing the solutionizing time (by 47\%), resulting in faster eutectic dissolution. Comparison of the aged microstructures reveals a similar distribution of precipitates between the classical Bridgman- and L-DED-processed samples.

title: RESYNC: Residual Latent-State Synchronization for Deadline-Bound Streaming Inference
abstract: Predicting every observation in a high-rate stream requires a model to finish before the next arrival. A large model may offer better predictions but miss that deadline. We propose RESYNC: the large model runs asynchronously, while a fast path updates its latest exact but stale latent state using the observations received since that state was computed and applies its unchanged prediction head. The updater learns from the frozen model's representations without task labels. Across one real and two synthetic streams and five architecture families, RESYNC beats the best compact or distilled alternative with a paired 95% interval above zero in all twelve dataset--architecture pairs with a material teacher advantage at anchor ages of 4--12 observations, and in eleven pairs at older tested ages up to 32. The share of the teacher's gain preserved remains complete on the real stream but is lower and generally declines with anchor age on the synthetic streams. In live replay with 1 ms arrivals, the synchronous large models cannot deliver any predictions on time while RESYNC serves at least 99.4% of arrivals within the interval, with 0.35--0.62 ms median latency on one CPU thread: around the same speed as or faster than the compact model, and 7.9--17.7$\times$ faster than synchronous large-model inference. RESYNC targets settings with background compute available but a strict per-observation response deadline.

title: Edge-scaling softening of a universal machine-learned potential: point-defect formation energies in a coronene graphene quantum dot
abstract: Universal machine-learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) are increasingly used as computationally efficient surrogates for density functional theory (DFT) in high-throughput nanomaterials screening. Systematic softening has been reported for several universal MLIPs when high-energy and far-from-equilibrium configurations are underrepresented in training data. We examine how this behavior appears at under-coordinated edge sites in graphene quantum dots (GQDs), where a vacancy can have pronounced molecular-radical character. Using coronene (C$_{24}$H$_{12}$), a hexagonal GQD with $D_{6h}$ symmetry and three carbon classes, we benchmark SevenNet (7net-omni-i12) against spin-polarized PBE DFT (GPAW) for monovacancy, divacancy, and Stone-Wales defects. Beyond the full site- and bond-resolved landscapes, we perform a controlled matched-reconstruction comparison in which 28 vacancy and divacancy configurations are scored by both engines using self-consistent chemical-potential reservoirs. In this dataset, SevenNet underestimates all 28 vacancy and divacancy formation energies, and the mean deficit increases with under-coordination within each defect family: 0.30-0.74 eV for monovacancies and 0.65-1.11 eV for divacancies as the number of broken edge C-H bonds increases. By contrast, the mean Stone-Wales energies differ by only 0.013 eV. SevenNet also preserves the ordering of three hydrogen-dependent reconstruction basins and reproduces $D_{6h}$-equivalent sites to within a few meV. The within-class symmetry spread therefore provides a practical diagnostic of basin-sensitive relaxations. Within the present coronene benchmark, these results support MLIP-based structure screening and preliminary ranking, while absolute vacancy energies and multi-basin edge configurations still require DFT validation.

title: Electron-Catalyzed Supramolecular Assembly with High Efficiency, Robustness, and Versatility
abstract: Although catalysis is widely exploited by nature to orchestrate noncovalent supramolecular assembly and build up complex living systems, its utilization in synthetic chemistry has conventionally been limited to accelerating covalent reactions. Consequently, the development of artificial systems for catalytic assembly remains a formidable and largely unexplored challenge. Here, we present a rationally designed strategy of electron-catalyzed supramolecular assembly, wherein the electron acts as an efficient, robust, and versatile catalyst to accelerate the formation of a donor–acceptor complex.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: Heavy Metal Pollution in Agricultural Soils: Source Identification, Risk-Based Remediation, and Safe Crop Production
abstract: Heavy metals in agricultural soils have been studied for half a century, but methods for measuring contamination remain far ahead of methods for turning a measurement into a decision. This review follows the problem as a chain from source identification through bioavailability and risk assessment to remediation and safe crop production, and asks at each link what the evidence can support. Three conclusions recur.

title: ScrewSense: Mapping the Invisible - Anomaly Detection and Error Classification in Screwdriving Processes
abstract: The growing volume of process data generated by screwdriving systems, combined with advancements in computing power, data storage, and algorithms, is facilitating the application of artificial intelligence in this field. Accurately detecting and classifying screwdriving errors is crucial for ensuring product quality, avoiding costly rework in manufacturing, and supporting sustainability by facilitating the maintenance, reuse, and recycling of screw-connected products. In this context, machine learning approaches offer a promising alternative to traditional monitoring techniques, such as window-based methods or envelope curves. This study examines the use of deep learning techniques for anomaly detection and error classification in screwdriving processes. The data corpus consists of multivariate time series capturing process parameters, such as torque and rotation angle. For anomaly detection, the embedding space of a vector quantized variational autoencoder was analyzed. In terms of error classification, four different model architectures were evaluated. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of anomaly detection and confirm that deep learning models can distinguish between multiple error categories beyond traditional binary classification. This extends the capabilities of conventional monitoring approaches, achieving accuracies of up to 100%. Additionally, real-world data material was examined in order to further demonstrate model robustness. Overall the results indicate strong generalization capability and highlight the practical potential of the developed models for use in industrial screwdriving processes, eliminating the need for expert knowledge in error identification and significantly reducing manual effort and analysis time.

title: Molecular Biomarkers and Biosensing Innovations for the Early Diagnosis of Ankylosing Spondylitis: From Molecular Mechanisms to Precision Diagnostics.
abstract: Ankylosing spondylitis is a chronic immune-mediated, inflammatory spondyloarthropathy in which delayed diagnosis remains a major clinical challenge, particularly during the early stages when definitive structural radiographic changes may be absent. Although HLA-B27 represents the most potent genetic association with ankylosing spondylitis, its incomplete penetrance and variability limit its use as a single diagnostic biomarker.
venue: The international journal of biochemistry & cell biology

title: Dynamics and Statistical Mechanics of Born-Oppenheimer Auxiliary Velocities
abstract: In Born-Oppenheimer (BO) dynamics, auxiliary variables such as electron densities, induced polarization and electrode charges follow stationarity conditions, yet their time derivatives, such as currents, are physical observables. Using Mass-Zero constrained dynamics, we interpret these derivatives as explicit dynamical variables and derive the invariant measure giving their equilibrium statistical properties. We illustrate the framework in constant-potential molecular dynamics, where the electrode-charge velocities reproduce BO current fluctuations and the frequency-dependent admittance.

title: Liquid-phase growth strategy densifies ceramic films at low temperature
abstract: Ceramic films are widely used in solid-state batteries, energy conversion devices and electronic systems. Their fabrication, however, often requires high-temperature sintering, which can cause elemental volatilization, compositional segregation and undesirable interfacial reactions. Achieving dense, compositionally uniform ceramic films at lower temperatures therefore remains a challenge.

title: Pumpkin seed protein puts a twist on nondairy coffee creamer
abstract: Pumpkin season is about more than cute décor. The squash contains lots of seeds with a high protein content, but they're usually discarded. Researchers reporting in ACS' Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry found another way to use the seeds, extracting that protein to create a plant-based coffee creamer. In initial taste tests, participants preferred the new creamer to a commercial nondairy option because it preserved the flavor and aroma of coffee better.

title: Dislocation Arrays Hosting Topological Bound States in Epitaxial Tetragonal FeSe Films
abstract: Topological defects in real space can host robust, localized quantum states for quantum information processing and sensing, yet deterministic control over their formation in crystalline materials remain challenging.

title: Proximal redox coupling enables oxidation damping for stable water electrolysis
abstract: Single-atom catalysts can mitigate reliance on scarce noble metals, but isolated sites can be fragile. Here a catalyst with proximal Ru−O−Cr motifs is fabricated that demonstrates proximal oxidation damping where the Cr neighbour buffers Ru overoxidation, improving stability for acidic oxygen evolution.

title: A Comprehensive Review of the Physics Involved in Modelling Transport Phenomena Associated with Extrusion-Deposition Additive Manufacturing Process
abstract: The dilemma of most upcoming researchers in the field of fiber reinforced polymer (FRP) composite processing is not the lack or accessibility to relevant background literature but rather their comprehensive nature, or their applicability to the specific needs of the researcher. Most existing literature either target just a specific modeling aspect or present high-level overview of the overall FRP process which lacks necessary underlying physics, coupling across hierarchical physics scales and computational techniques needed to improve on existing process simulation tools without necessarily…

title: The global distribution of plant diversity.
abstract: Recent developments in biodiversity research have considerably advanced our understanding of the global distribution of plant diversity. This synthesis reviews current knowledge on plant distribution patterns and their drivers, highlighting methodological innovations such as remote sensing, artificial intelligence, machine learning and mechanistic modelling for quantifying plant diversity and uncovering its causes.

title: Large Pockels Effect in Multiaxial Ferroelectrics Induced by Polarization Reorientation
abstract: Materials with large linear electro-optic (Pockels) effect have significant potential for fabricating energy-efficient photonic devices. Previous strategies have mostly relied on structural softness---associated with phase boundary, domain wall, or strain induced phase transition---to create large Pockels effect in ferroelectrics. In this Letter, we show that polarization reorientation in multiaxial ferroelectrics may create structural softness and thus induce large Pockels effect. By developing a phenomenological theory, we find that multiaxial ferroelectrics exhibit a hysteretic relationship between the azimuth angles of the polarization and the electric field, and a possible divergence of the linear electro-optic coefficient may occur at an appropriate polarization azimuth angle. This suggests a brand-new strategy for engineering large Pockels effect in multiaxial ferroelectrics. We perform first-principles simulations on several multiaxial ferroelectrics and predict that polarization reorientation can significantly enhance the electro-optic coefficients in monolayer SnSe and bulk KNbO$_3$. This validates the soundness of our strategy and emphasizes multiaxial ferroelectrics as promising platforms toward large Pockels effect.

title: Metric random tilings: exact entropy and the diffraction of counted disorder
abstract: Tiling mathematics has twice become the language of a state of matter: crystals, then quasicrystals, whose thermodynamics are described by the random tiling of fixed shapes. There the counted variable is the arrangement rather than the geometry, although the metric is what chemical design sets and diffraction measures. Here we introduce metric random tilings, periodic networks of locked topology whose edge lengths fluctuate under exact face closure, so that the geometry itself is countable. Purpose-built counting engines enumerate Kepler's eleven uniform networks and divide them into seven zero-entropy ones and four carriers with positive metric entropy, each certified by an explicit construction. On the honeycomb, the densest carrier, all edge-length value domains considered carry extensive entropy, with the arithmetic class reaching $s = 0.544\,k_B$ per tile (fit band 0.53--0.58), the other two $\approx 0.2$. In diffraction, translational increase of the value domain leaves the entropy exactly invariant while the coherent fraction of the Bragg intensity at fixed patch size varies from $9\times10^{-4}$ to 0.58, following the Debye--Waller law of the amplitude flow. Metric disorder thus enters the exact-counting paradigm, and is identifiable in real materials by Bragg spots wrapped in metric halos.

title: Tailored magnetic domain-wall ratchet effects through density gradients in triangular-hole arrays
abstract: We investigate domain wall (DW) dynamics and morphology in amorphous Co$_{0.86}$Zr$_{0.14}$ thin films patterned with engineered, density-graded triangular-hole arrays. Using Kerr microscopy and high-resolution XMCD-PEEM imaging, we demonstrate that DW propagation is governed by the interplay between hole orientation, density gradients, and local magnetostatic interactions. In cooperative configurations, the density gradient reinforces the geometric ratchet effect, whereas in competing configurations, the two mechanisms oppose each other, leading to an inverse ratchet and enabling experimental access to backward DW propagation. Remarkably, density-graded arrays substantially reduce the stochastic variability of depinning fields observed in periodic arrays, resulting in highly reproducible DW motion. The depinning fields are described by a rigid DW model and an empirical scaling law incorporating both inter-hole spacing and array periodicity. These results demonstrate that engineered density gradients provide an effective route to deterministic control of DW propagation, with potential applications in spintronic and neuromorphic devices.

title: Systematic Evaluation of Training Data Generation Strategies for Machine Learning-Based Molecular and Materials Property Prediction
abstract: Machine-learning (ML) models for molecular and materials property prediction are often trained on large datasets curated through arbitrary or generic sampling strategies. Such approaches can lead to the over- or under-representation of regions of chemical and materials space that are most relevant to the prediction task. An important challenge is therefore how to efficiently curate training data to maximize predictive performance while minimising the number of labelled examples required. Here, we systematically compare training data acquisition strategies for molecular and materials property prediction, ranging from random sampling to various active learning approaches. We evaluate their performance across different model classes, representations, datasets, and target properties. Our results show that the effectiveness of data acquisition strategies depend strongly on the interplay between the model, dataset, and prediction task, although uncertainty-based sampling generally outperforms alternative strategies. Based on these findings, we derive guidelines for selecting data acquisition strategies under a given labelling budget.

title: Empowering HFIP as a Radical Trifluoromethylating Reagent by Photoelectrochemical Iron Catalysis
abstract: The development of practical synthetic methods for incorporating trifluoromethyl (CF3) groups into organic scaffolds is of paramount importance in medicinal chemistry, as such modifications profoundly modulate the physicochemical properties of drug candidates. 1,1,1,3,3,3-Hexafluoro-2-propanol (HFIP) is widely utilized as a unique solvent in synthetic chemistry and also represents a promising CF3 source due to its high availability and low cost.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society

title: DeepRelCDR: A Deep Relation-Aware Molecular Graph Attention Framework for Cancer Drug Response Prediction
abstract: Predicting cancer cell-line response to therapeutic compounds is central to precision oncology, yet graph neural network models typically represent each drug only through covalent-bond connectivity, leaving ring-system and functional-group structure implicit; the relation set used here is fixed by chemical domain knowledge and evaluated on a single pharmacoge-nomic resource rather than learned or validated across cohorts.

title: Protein Language Models Fail To Capture Contact Predictions Under Invariant Relabeling
abstract: Protein language models (pLMs) produce highly accurate contact maps from single-sequence inputs. People often take this accuracy as proof that these models implicitly learn invariant coevolutionary statistics, extracting the same signals as classical alignment-based methods like Potts. In this work, we introduce a diagnostic framework around a global bijective relabeling of the amino-acid alphabet. This transformation permutes residue letters while leaving all alignment-level information, column entropies, and pairwise edit distances unchanged. Pseudolikelihood Potts models and inverse-covariance estimators remain invariant under this transformation, but pLMs fail the test. Across multiple architectures (ESM-2, MSA Transformer, AMPLIFY) and model scales (8M to 3B parameters), pLM contact maps collapse under arbitrary relabeling. Using Hamming distance controls and biochemical grouping interventions, we attempt to isolate what likely causes this degradation and find that these models rely on explicit, canonical residue identities (``alphabet anchoring'') rather than pure coevolutionary statistics. Increasing scale makes models more responsive to biochemical classes, but their performance still degrades under relabeling. Our findings show a gap between how pLMs and classical coevolutionary models compute contacts. More broadly, our work shows how diagnostic perturbations that leave classical models provably unchanged can expose hidden representation biases and prevent over-reliance on neural black boxes in biological modeling.

title: Two Unconventional Hall Effects in the Kagome Magnet TmMn4Cr$_2$Sn$_6$
abstract: We identify two Hall anomalies in the kagome magnet TmMn$_4$Cr$_2$Sn$_6$. We propose that the high-field anomaly reflects a discontinuous spin reorientation and differing sublattice contributions to Hall transport and magnetization. At low fields, Hall hysteresis persists despite negligible magnetic hysteresis, suggesting a chirality-related contribution, although its microscopic origin remains unresolved. These contrasting regimes show how magnetic transitions can mimic unconventional Hall signals and highlight the limits of magnetization-based Hall decomposition.

title: Accurate quantum chemical property prediction with transferable electron-density representations
abstract: Machine-learning models of molecules usually encode nuclear geometry, while spatial electronic information is either omitted or requires costly molecule-specific quantum calculations. Here we present eMol, an electron-density-driven model that overcomes this trade-off by coupling atomic scaffolds with density-derived probes via a retrievable memory, allowing compatible electronic environments to be reused across molecules without repeated first-principles density calculations.

title: Algebraic Diagrammatic Construction of the Multichannel Dyson Equation
abstract: The multichannel Dyson equation (MCDE) was recently introduced as a new approximation scheme to compute the one-body Green’s function [Riva et al. Phys. Rev. Lett.2023, 131, 216401.] in many-body systems. The physical content of this novel approximation scheme is further clarified by recovering it from (an extended version of) the algebraic diagrammatic construction (ADC) truncation scheme. It is thus demonstrated that the MCDE approximation lies in between the so-called ADC(2) and ADC(3) truncations of the dynamical self-energy.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: Multireference QM/MM Nonadiabatic Dynamics with Quantum Nuclei in Explicit Environment: Implementation in COBRAMM and Application to the Sub-100 fs Energy Transfer in NADH
abstract: We present a mixed quantum-classical framework for simulating nonadiabatic excited-state dynamics in explicit environments. The method combines a fully quantum-mechanical treatment of both electronic and nuclear degrees of freedom in the high-level (HL) region with classical propagation of the surrounding low-level (LL) environment. The HL dynamics is described using a linear vibronic coupling Hamiltonian parametrized at the multireference (XMS-CASPT2) level of theory, while bidirectional systembath coupling is incorporated through a dynamically updated electrostatic embedding scheme. The implementation, integrated into the COBRAMM suite, interfaces Quantics, OpenMolcas, and AMBER. Benchmark tests assess the stability, energy conservation, and approximations underlying the protocol. Among those, we highlight the crude adiabatic approximation, which allows to avoid explicit QM calculations for the update of the Hamiltonian during the dynamics, making the simulation time dependent only on the size of the active space required for the initial parametrization. As a proof of concept, we investigate the sub-100 fs excitation energy transfer (EET) in solvated NADH. Compared to simulations with a frozen environment, the explicit dynamical response of the solvent enhances the charge transfer (CT)-mediated EET pathway. The results highlight the critical role of fast librational solvent modes in ultrafast nonadiabatic phenomena and establish the presented protocol as a robust approach for treating environment-driven internal conversion in rigid photoresponsive molecular systems.
venue: Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation

title: Knowledge Graph-Based Hypothesis Generation and Experimental Validation in Yeast
abstract: Integrating biological knowledge with automated experimentation enables the generation and testing of hypotheses for scientific discovery. However, identifying promising hypotheses from heterogeneous biological data remains challenging.
