Here, we present a knowledge graph-based approach to prioritising gene-chemical interactions associated with decreased chemical stress resistance in the yeast Saccharomyces cerevisiae. We combine information from biological databases and ontologies with a hierarchy-aware graph neural network to rank candidate interactions for experimental testing.

title: Nigeria’s first Ebola case in a decade has the nation on high alert
abstract: Africa’s most populous country faces health-care challenges, particularly in preparedness

title: From bush food to biodegradable materials: Unlocking the potential of pigface
abstract: An Australian native plant traditionally used by Indigenous communities for food and medicine could help scientists develop stronger, more flexible biodegradable film. UNSW researchers have discovered that adding extracts from pigface, Carpobrotus glaucescens, a hardy coastal succulent, to seaweed-based films can significantly improve their strength and flexibility.

title: Case-Based Teaching in Veterinary Parasitology: Changes in Knowledge and Student- Reported Engagement, Conceptual Understanding, and Clinical Reasoning
abstract: Background Veterinary parasitology requires students to integrate biological concepts with epidemiological interpretation, diagnostic reasoning, and disease-control decision-making. Predominantly lecture-based instruction may provide fewer opportunities to apply theoretical knowledge to authentic clinical and field situations. This study examined the implementation of contextually relevant case-based teaching as an active-learning strategy in undergraduate veterinary parasitology and considered its contribution to broader STEM education.

title: What a brewery can teach the chemical industry
abstract: What do you do when the chemical you want to make is toxic to the microbe making it? It is a problem that limits efforts to replace oil-based manufacturing with biology, and one that researchers in the Sustainable Commodity Chemicals through Enzyme Engineering and Design project are approaching by borrowing a principle from brewing.

title: CROWN: Curated Repository of Well-Resolved Noncovalent Interactions
abstract: The usefulness of structural data sets for machine-learning models of protein–ligand recognition depends not only on their size, but also on how structural imperfections are handled. Existing resources typically trade structural rigor for scale. Recent data sets such as SPINDR improve large-scale structural data through systematic preprocessing, but restrictive inclusion criteria still discard much of the chemical and biological complexity represented in the Protein Data Bank (PDB).
venue: Journal of Chemical Information and Modeling

title: Primer: An AI Framework for Instructor-Centered Educational Simulation Creation
abstract: Educational simulations are a well-established pedagogical technique that gives learners opportunities to apply knowledge, respond to challenges, and reflect on their performance. High-quality simulations, however, are difficult to build, requiring instructor input, scenario design, character development, scaffolding, technical implementation, and repeated revision. This paper presents Primer, an open-source, LLM-agnostic AI-supported system that helps educators create adaptive educational simulations. Educators contribute their knowledge of the subject, lesson, and students, while generative AI produces responsive variations of practice for students. Primer uses a multi-agent system centered around executing educator's instructional intent through the entire learning experience. We hope that by releasing Primer as an open-source system, including its prompts and GitHub repository, we provide a foundation for development and research on educator-in-the-loop AI authoring, multi-agent educational workflows, and simulation-based pedagogy. Further, by allowing the use of various AI models, including local and open source models, we provide the opportunity for implementation under varied governance regimes. Primer points toward a model of educational AI in which instructors can create locally grounded practice opportunities based on their own materials, goals, examples, and knowledge of students.

title: Cyclative Carbon Quaternization of Alkyl Boronic Esters via Copper-Catalyzed Aminyl Radical Transfer
abstract: Despite the rich chemistry of alkyl boronic esters (alkyl Bpins) in C–B bond transformations, carbon quaternization via concurrent C–B and C–H bond scission on the boron-substituted carbon has remained elusive. Herein, we report a copper-catalyzed aminyl radical-mediated cyclative C-quaternization of alkyl Bpins with acrylamides to access valuable carbo- and spirocyclic scaffolds. Central to this transformation is a sequential C–B/C–H bond-cleavage, in which ART triggers C–B cleavage and HAT enables site-selective C–H functionalization.
